Generate Token with Password Grant at Custom Token Endpoint

overview: The authz-casdoor Plugin can be used to add centralized authentication with Casdoor .

route.callback_url: Callback URL used to receive state and code.

overview: The wolf-rbac Plugin provides a role-based access control system with wolf to a Route or a Service. This Plugin can be used with a Consumer .

route.appid: App id added in wolf console. This field supports saving the value in Secret Manager using the APISIX Secret resource.
route.header_prefix: Prefix for a custom HTTP header. After authentication is successful, three headers will be added to the request header (for backend) and response header (for frontend) namely: X-UserId , X-Username , and X-Nickname .

overview: The openid-connect Plugin supports the integration with OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers, such as Keycloak, Auth0, Microsoft Entra ID, Google, Okta, and more. It allows APISIX to authenticate clients and obtain their information from the identity provider before allowing or denying their access to upstream protected resources.

route.discovery: URL to the well-known discovery document of the OpenID provider, which contains a list of OP API endpoints. The Plugin can directly utilize the endpoints from the discovery document. You can also configure these endpoints individually, which takes precedence over the endpoints supplied in the discovery document.
route.scope: OIDC scope that corresponds to information that should be returned about the authenticated user, also known as claims . This is used to authorize users with proper permission. The default value is openid , the required scope for OIDC to return a sub claim that uniquely identifies the authenticated user. Additional scopes can be appended and delimited by spaces, such as openid email profile .
route.required_scopes: Scopes required to be present in the access token. If any required scope is missing, the Plugin rejects the request with a 403 forbidden error. In the authorization code flow, the granted scopes are read from the scope claim of the access token, falling back to the claim of the ID token when the access token carries none; a session whose granted scopes cannot be determined either way is rejected.
route.realm: Realm in WWW-Authenticate response header accompanying a 401 unauthorized request due to invalid bearer token.
route.bearer_only: If true, strictly require bearer access token in requests for authentication.
route.post_logout_redirect_uri: URL to redirect users to after the logout_path receives a request to log out.
route.redirect_uri: URI to redirect to after authentication with the OpenID provider. Note that the redirect URI should not be the same as the request URI, but a sub-path of the request URI. For example, if the uri of the Route is /api/v1/* , redirect_uri can be configured as /api/v1/redirect . If redirect_uri is not configured, APISIX will append /.apisix/redirect to the request URI to determine the value for redirect_uri . It is recommended to set redirect_uri to an absolute URL (with scheme and host). This makes the value fixed instead of assembled from request headers, so a forged Host or Forwarded header cannot influence the redirect URI sent to the identity provider.
route.timeout: Request timeout time in seconds.
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify the OpenID provider’s SSL certificates. Note: The default value was changed from false to true in APISIX 3.16.0. This is a breaking change. If you are upgrading from an earlier version, ensure your OpenID provider’s SSL certificate is valid or explicitly set this to false to preserve previous behavior.
route.introspection_endpoint: URL of the token introspection endpoint for the OpenID provider used to introspect access tokens. If this is unset, the introspection endpoint presented in the well-known discovery document is used as a fallback .
route.introspection_endpoint_auth_method: Authentication method for the token introspection endpoint. The value should be one of the authentication methods specified in the introspection_endpoint_auth_methods_supported authorization server metadata as seen in the well-known discovery document, such as client_secret_basic , client_secret_post , private_key_jwt , and client_secret_jwt .
route.token_endpoint_auth_method: Authentication method for the token endpoint. The value should be one of the authentication methods specified in the token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported authorization server metadata as seen in the well-known discovery document, such as client_secret_basic , client_secret_post , private_key_jwt , and client_secret_jwt . If the configured method is not supported, fall back to the first method in the token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported array.
route.public_key: Public key used to verify JWT signature if asymmetric algorithm is used. Providing this value to perform token verification will skip token introspection in client credentials flow. You can pass the public key in -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\n……\n-----END PUBLIC KEY----- format.
route.use_jwks: If true and if public_key is not set, use the JWKS to verify JWT signature and skip token introspection in client credentials flow. The JWKS endpoint is parsed from the discovery document.
route.use_pkce: If true, use the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) for Authorization Code Flow as defined in RFC 7636 .
route.par.enabled: If true, use OAuth 2.0 Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR) as defined in RFC 9126 . Authorization request parameters are sent to the PAR endpoint and the browser is redirected with the returned request_uri .
route.par.endpoint: URL of the PAR endpoint. If unset, the endpoint from the well-known discovery document is used.
route.par.endpoint_auth_method: Authentication method for the PAR endpoint. If unset, token_endpoint_auth_method is used. private_key_jwt requires client_rsa_private_key and client_secret_jwt requires client_secret ; unlike the token endpoint, the PAR request fails outright when the method it is given cannot be used.
route.dpop.enabled: If true, use OAuth 2.0 DPoP as defined in RFC 9449 . The Plugin sends DPoP proof JWTs to the token endpoint and uses DPoP-bound access tokens for user info requests.
route.dpop.signing_alg: Signing algorithm for DPoP proof JWTs.
route.dpop.private_key: PEM-encoded private key used to sign DPoP proof JWTs. Required when dpop.enabled is true.
route.dpop.public_jwk: Public JWK that matches dpop.private_key . Required when dpop.enabled is true. The JWK must not contain private key material.
route.token_signing_alg_values_expected: Algorithm used for signing JWT, such as RS256 .
route.set_access_token_header: If true, set the access token in a request header. By default, the X-Access-Token header is used.
route.access_token_in_authorization_header: If true and if set_access_token_header is also true, set the access token in the Authorization header.
route.set_id_token_header: If true and if the ID token is available, set the value in the X-ID-Token request header. Note: this header contains base64(JSON(decoded_claims)) and carries no cryptographic signature.
route.set_raw_id_token_header: If true and if the raw signed ID token JWT is available, set the value in the X-Raw-ID-Token request header. Unlike X-ID-Token , this header contains the original RS256-signed JWT from the identity provider and can be verified against the provider’s JWKS endpoint. The plugin automatically persists the raw JWT in the session when this option is enabled.
route.set_userinfo_header: If true and if user info data is available, set the value in the X-Userinfo request header.
route.set_refresh_token_header: If true and if the refresh token is available, set the value in the X-Refresh-Token request header.
route.session: Session configuration used when bearer_only is false and the Plugin uses Authorization Code flow.
route.session.secret: Key used for session encryption and HMAC operation when bearer_only is false .
route.session.cookie_name: Session cookie name. Forwarded to lua-resty-session 4.x as cookie_name .
route.session.cookie_path: Cookie path scope. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as cookie_path .
route.session.cookie_domain: Cookie domain scope. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as cookie_domain .
route.session.cookie_secure: If true, set the Secure cookie attribute. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as cookie_secure .
route.session.cookie_http_only: If true, set the HttpOnly cookie attribute. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as cookie_http_only .
route.session.cookie_same_site: SameSite cookie attribute. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as cookie_same_site .
route.session.idling_timeout: Idling timeout in seconds. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as idling_timeout .
route.session.rolling_timeout: Rolling timeout in seconds. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as rolling_timeout .
route.session.absolute_timeout: Absolute session lifetime in seconds. Forwarded to lua-resty-session as absolute_timeout .
route.session.cookie.lifetime: Deprecated. Mapped to session.absolute_timeout at runtime when absolute_timeout is not set. Use session.absolute_timeout instead.
route.session.redis: Redis configuration when storage is redis .
route.session.redis.ssl_verify: Verify SSL certificate for Redis connection.
route.session_contents: Session content configurations. If unconfigured, all data will be stored in the session.
route.session_contents.access_token: If true, store the access token in the session.
route.session_contents.id_token: If true, store the ID token in the session.
route.session_contents.enc_id_token: If true, store the encrypted ID token in the session.
route.session_contents.user: If true, store the user info in the session.
route.unauth_action: Action for unauthenticated requests. When set to auth , redirect to the authentication endpoint of the OpenID provider. When set to pass , allow the request without authentication. When set to deny , return 401 unauthenticated responses rather than start the authorization code grant flow.
route.proxy_opts: Configurations for the proxy server that the OpenID provider is behind.
route.proxy_opts.http_proxy: Proxy server address for HTTP requests, such as http://<proxy_host>:<proxy_port> .
route.proxy_opts.https_proxy: Proxy server address for HTTPS requests, such as http://<proxy_host>:<proxy_port> .
route.proxy_opts.http_proxy_authorization: Default Proxy-Authorization header value to be used with http_proxy . Can be overridden with custom Proxy-Authorization request header.
route.proxy_opts.https_proxy_authorization: Default Proxy-Authorization header value to be used with https_proxy . Cannot be overridden with custom Proxy-Authorization request header since with HTTPS, the authorization is completed when connecting.
route.proxy_opts.no_proxy: Comma-separated list of hosts that should not be proxied.
route.authorization_params: Additional parameters to send in the request to the authorization endpoint.
route.client_rsa_private_key: Client private key used to sign the client assertion JWT for authentication to the OP. Required whenever private_key_jwt is selected, by token_endpoint_auth_method , introspection_endpoint_auth_method or par.endpoint_auth_method . The key type has to match client_jwt_assertion_alg : RSA for the RS* algorithms, and an EC key on the matching curve for the ES* ones.
route.client_rsa_private_key_id: Client private key ID used to compute the signed client assertion JWT. Optional whenever private_key_jwt is selected.
route.client_jwt_assertion_expires_in: Life duration of the signed JWT for authentication to the OP, in seconds. Used whenever private_key_jwt or client_secret_jwt is selected, for the token, introspection or PAR endpoint.
route.client_jwt_assertion_alg: Signing algorithm for the client assertion JWT. Defaults to RS256 for private_key_jwt and HS256 for client_secret_jwt . Use a HS* algorithm with client_secret_jwt and an asymmetric one with private_key_jwt ; an asymmetric algorithm also has to match client_rsa_private_key , which must be an EC key on P-256 for ES256 and on P-521 for ES512 . This is one algorithm for every endpoint, so a configuration cannot select private_key_jwt for one endpoint and client_secret_jwt for another while setting it. When the discovery document advertises token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported , the configured value must also be supported by the OP.
route.client_jwt_assertion_audience: Audience for the client assertion JWT. If unset, the endpoint URL being called is used. Configure this when APISIX reaches the token endpoint through an internal URL but the OP expects its external token endpoint URL as the audience.
route.renew_access_token_on_expiry: If true, attempt to silently renew the access token when it expires or if a refresh token is available. If the token fails to renew, redirect user for re-authentication.
route.access_token_expires_in: Lifetime of the access token in seconds if no expires_in attribute is present in the token endpoint response.
route.refresh_session_interval: Time interval in seconds to refresh user ID token without requiring re-authentication. When not set, it will not check the expiration time of the session issued to the client by the gateway.
route.iat_slack: Tolerance of clock skew in seconds with the iat claim in an ID token.
route.accept_none_alg: Set to true if the OpenID provider does not sign its ID token, such as when the signature algorithm is set to none .
route.accept_unsupported_alg: If true, ignore ID token signature to accept unsupported signature algorithm.
route.access_token_expires_leeway: Expiration leeway in seconds for access token renewal. When set to a value greater than 0, token renewal will take place the set amount of time before token expiration. This avoids errors in case the access token just expires when arriving to the resource server.
route.force_reauthorize: If true, execute the authorization flow even when a token has been cached.
route.use_nonce: If true, enable nonce parameter in authorization request.
route.revoke_tokens_on_logout: If true, notify the authorization server that a previously obtained refresh or access token is no longer needed at the revocation endpoint.
route.jwk_expires_in: Expiration time for JWK cache in seconds.
route.jwt_verification_cache_ignore: If true, force re-verification for a bearer token and ignore any existing cached verification results.
route.cache_segment: Optional name of a cache segment, used to separate and differentiate caches used by token introspection or JWT verification.
route.introspection_interval: TTL of the cached and introspected access token in seconds. The default value is 0, which means this option is not used and the Plugin defaults to use the TTL passed by expiry claim defined in introspection_expiry_claim . If introspection_interval is larger than 0 and less than the TTL passed by expiry claim defined in introspection_expiry_claim , use introspection_interval .
route.introspection_expiry_claim: Name of the expiry claim, which controls the TTL of the cached and introspected access token.
route.introspection_addon_headers: Used to append additional header values to the introspection HTTP request. If the specified header does not exist in the origin request, the value will not be appended.
route.claim_validator.issuer.valid_issuers: An array of trusted JWT issuers. If unconfigured, the issuer returned by the discovery endpoint will be used, and a token is rejected while the discovery document cannot be fetched, since no trusted issuer is known then.
route.claim_validator.audience.claim: Name of the claim that contains the audience.
route.claim_validator.audience.required: If true, audience claim is required and the name of the claim will be the name defined in claim .
route.claim_validator.audience.match_with_clie: If true, require the audience to match the client ID. If the audience is a string, it must exactly match the client ID. If the audience is an array of strings, at least one of the values must match the client ID. If no match is found, you will receive a mismatched audience error. A token without the audience claim is rejected too, as it cannot match the client ID. This requirement is stated in the OpenID Connect specification to ensure that the token is intended for the specific client.
route.claim_schema: JSON schema of OIDC response claim. Example: {"type":"object","properties":{"access_token":{"type":"string"}},"required":["access_token"]} - validates that the response contains a required string field access_token .

examples.title: Authorization Code Flow with PAR and DPoP

overview:
The cas-auth Plugin can be used to access CAS (Central Authentication Service 2.0) IdP (Identity Provider)
to do authentication, from the SP (service provider) perspective.

route.cas_callback_uri: redirect uri used to callback the SP from IdP after login or logout.
route.cookie: configuration for the cookies the plugin issues during the CAS login flow.
route.cookie.secret: secret (32+ characters) used to sign the request URI cookie. The same value must be configured on every APISIX node. Generate with e.g. openssl rand -base64 48 .
route.cookie.secure: whether to set the Secure attribute on the issued cookies. Set to false only for deployments where the protected route is not served over HTTPS (e.g. internal-only or development environments).
route.cookie.samesite: value for the SameSite cookie attribute. Allowed values are "Lax" and "None" ; "Strict" is intentionally not supported because it breaks the IdP→SP redirect when the IdP is on a different site.

overview: The hmac-auth Plugin supports HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) authentication as a mechanism to ensure the integrity of requests, preventing them from being modified during transmissions. To use the Plugin, you would configure HMAC secret keys on Consumers and enable the Plugin on Routes or Services.

When a Consumer is successfully authenticated, APISIX adds additional headers, such as X-Consumer-Username , X-Credential-Identifier , and other Consumer custom headers if configured, to the request, before proxying it to the Upstream service. The Upstream service will be able to differentiate between consumers and implement additional logic as needed. If any of these values is not available, the corresponding header will not be added.

consumer.key_id: Unique identifier for the HMAC credential/key, used as keyId in the Signature Authorization header to identify the associated credential configuration such as the secret key.
consumer.secret_key: Secret key used to generate an HMAC. This field supports saving the value in Secret Manager using the APISIX Secret resource.

route.allowed_algorithms: The list of HMAC algorithms allowed.
route.clock_skew: Maximum allowable difference in seconds between the value of the request’s Date header (which must be in GMT format) and APISIX’s current time. This helps reject stale requests when the client and server clocks are reasonably in sync. For the freshness window to be meaningful, date must be part of signed_headers so that the Date value is bound into the signing string. With the default signed_headers value of ["date"] , this binding is in place out of the box.
route.signed_headers: The list of headers that must be included in the client request’s HMAC signing string. The default value of ["date"] ensures the Date header is always bound into the signing string, so that the value used for the clock_skew freshness check is itself covered by the HMAC. Set this explicitly to override the headers that must be signed; setting it to an empty array [] removes the requirement entirely.
route.validate_request_body: If true, validate the integrity of the request body to ensure it has not been tampered with during transmission. Specifically, the Plugin creates a SHA-256 base64-encoded digest and compares it to the Digest header. If the Digest header is missing or if the digests do not match, the validation fails.
route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes that the Plugin reads into memory to validate the digest when validate_request_body is true . Requests whose body exceeds this limit are rejected with 413 . Prevents unbounded memory buffering of large request bodies.
route.hide_credentials: If true, do not pass the authorization request header to Upstream services.
route.anonymous_consumer: Anonymous Consumer name. If configured, allow anonymous users to bypass the authentication.
route.realm: Realm in the WWW-Authenticate response header returned with a 401 Unauthorized response due to authentication failure.

examples.title: Implement HMAC Authentication on a Route

overview: The authz-casbin Plugin is an authorization Plugin based on Lua Casbin . This Plugin supports powerful authorization scenarios based on various access control models .

route.model_path: Path of the Casbin model configuration file.
route.policy_path: Path of the Casbin policy file.
route.model: Casbin model configuration in text format.
route.username: Header in the request that will be used in the request to pass the username (subject).

overview: The ldap-auth Plugin can be used to add LDAP authentication to a Route or a Service.
This Plugin works with the Consumer object and the consumers of the API can authenticate with an LDAP server using basic authentication .

consumer.user_dn: User dn of the LDAP client. For example, cn=user01,ou=users,dc=example,dc=org . This field supports saving the value in Secret Manager using the APISIX Secret resource.

route.base_dn: Base dn of the LDAP server. For example, ou=users,dc=example,dc=org .
route.use_tls: If set to true uses TLS.
route.tls_verify: Whether to verify the server certificate when use_tls is enabled; If set to true , you must set ssl_trusted_certificate in config.yaml , and make sure the host of ldap_uri matches the host in server certificate.
route.hide_credentials: If true, do not pass the Authorization request header to the Upstream service. The header carries the directory password, which is usually reusable beyond this API.
route.realm: The realm to include in the WWW-Authenticate header when authentication fails.

overview: The jwe-decrypt Plugin reads a five-part compact token from a request header, selects a Consumer by the token’s kid , decrypts the ciphertext with AES-256-GCM, and writes the plaintext to a configured header before proxying the request. You can enable the Plugin on APISIX Routes or Services .

The token uses JWE Compact Serialization with the dir key management algorithm and the A256GCM content encryption algorithm, so a token produced by a standard JWE library is accepted. Configure a 32-byte decryption secret on the Consumer.

consumer.key: A unique key that identifies the Credential for a Consumer.
consumer.secret: A shared symmetric key. Use a secret reference , such as $env://... or $secret://... .
consumer.is_base64_encoded: Set to true if the secret is base64url encoded. The decoded secret must still be 32 bytes.

route.header: The header to get the token from.
route.forward_header: Name of the header that passes the plaintext to the Upstream.
route.strict: If true, return a 403 error when the JWE token is missing. If false, continue when the token is not found.

examples.title: Create a Consumer with the Decryption Key

overview: The multi-auth Plugin allows Consumers using different authentication methods to share the same Route or Service. It supports the configuration of multiple authentication Plugins, so that a request would be allowed through if it authenticates successfully against any configured authentication method.

When every configured method fails, the request is rejected with a 401 and each method’s underlying failure reason is written to the error log (for example, key-auth failed to authenticate the request, code: 401. error: failed to find consumer: invalid api key ), which helps diagnose why a particular authentication method rejected the request.

route.auth_plugins: An array of at least two authentication Plugins.

examples.title: Allow Different Authentications on the Same Route

overview: The opa Plugin supports the integration with Open Policy Agent (OPA) , a unified policy engine and framework that helps define and enforce authorization policies. Authorization logic is defined in Rego and stored in OPA.
Once configured, the OPA engine will evaluate the client request to a protected Route to determine whether the request should have access to the Upstream resource based on the defined policies.

route.policy: Policy path to evaluate. The plugin appends this value to /v1/data/<policy> , so it must point to an OPA document/decision whose result is an object containing an allow field. The returned object can also include reason , headers , and status_code . For example, use a path such as rbac only if querying /v1/data/rbac returns an object with this structure, rather than a bare boolean result.
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify the OPA server’s SSL certificate.
route.timeout: Timeout for the HTTP call in milliseconds.
route.keepalive: If true, keep the connection alive for multiple requests.
route.keepalive_timeout: Idle time in milliseconds after which the connection is closed.
route.with_route: If true, send information of the current Route.
route.with_service: If true, send information of the current Service.
route.with_consumer: If true, send information of the current Consumer. Note that the Consumer information may include sensitive information such as the API key. Only set this option to true if you are sure it is safe to do so.
route.send_headers_upstream: List of header names to forward from the OPA response to the Upstream service when the request is allowed.

overview: The forward-auth Plugin supports the integration with an external authorization service for authentication and authorization. If the authentication fails, a customizable error message will be returned to the client. If the authentication succeeds, the request will be forwarded to the Upstream service along with the following request headers that APISIX added:

route.uri: URI of the external authorization service.
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify the authorization service’s SSL certificate.
route.request_method: HTTP method APISIX uses to send requests to the external authorization service. When set to POST , APISIX will send POST requests along with the request body to the external authorization service. If the authorization decision depends on request parameters from a POST body, it is recommended to extract the necessary fields using $post_arg.* and pass them via the extra_headers field instead.
route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered and forwarded to the external authorization service when request_method is POST . Requests whose body exceeds this limit are rejected with 413 . Prevents unbounded memory buffering of large request bodies.
route.request_headers: Client request headers that should be forwarded to the external authorization service. If not configured, only headers added by APISIX are forwarded, such as X-Forwarded-* .
route.upstream_headers: External authorization service response headers that should be forwarded to the Upstream service. If not configured, no headers are forwarded to the Upstream service.
route.client_headers: External authorization service response headers that should be forwarded to the client when authentication fails. If not configured, no headers are forwarded to the client.
route.extra_headers: Additional headers to send to the authorization service. Support NGINX variables in values.
route.timeout: Timeout for the external authorization service HTTP call in milliseconds.
route.keepalive: If true, keep the connections open for multiple requests.
route.keepalive_timeout: Idle time in milliseconds after which the established HTTP connections will be closed.
route.keepalive_pool: Maximum number of connections in the connection pool.
route.allow_degradation: If true, allow APISIX to continue handling requests without the Plugin when the Plugin or its dependencies become unavailable.
route.status_on_error: HTTP status code to return to the client when there is a network error with the external authorization service.

examples.title: Forward Designated Headers to Upstream Resource
Return Designated Headers to Clients on Authentication Failure

overview: The cors Plugin allows you to enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) . CORS is an HTTP-header based mechanism which allows a server to specify any origins (domain, scheme, or port) other than its own, and instructs browsers to allow the loading of resources from those origins.

route.allow_origins: Comma-separated string of origins to allow CORS, in the format scheme://host:port , for example https://somedomain.com:8081 . If you have multiple origins, use , to list them. If allow_credential is set to false , you can use * to allow all origins. If allow_credential is set to true , you can use ** to forcefully allow all origins, but this poses security risks.
route.allow_methods: Comma-separated string of HTTP request methods to allow CORS, for example GET , POST . If allow_credential is set to false , you can use * to allow all methods. If allow_credential is set to true , you can use ** to forcefully allow all methods, but this poses security risks.
route.allow_headers: Comma-separated string of HTTP headers allowed in requests when accessing a cross-origin resource. If allow_credential is set to false , you can use * to allow all request headers. If allow_credential is set to true , you can use ** to forcefully allow all request headers, but this poses security risks.
route.expose_headers: Comma-separated string of HTTP headers that should be made available in response to a cross-origin request. If allow_credential is set to false , you can use * to allow all response headers. If not specified, the Plugin will not modify the Access-Control-Expose-Headers header. See Access-Control-Expose-Headers - MDN for more details.
route.max_age: Maximum time in seconds for which the results of a preflight request can be cached. If the time is within this limit, the browser will check the cached result. Set to -1 to disable caching. Note that the maximum value is browser-dependent. See Access-Control-Max-Age for more details.
route.allow_credential: When set to true , allows requests to include credentials such as cookies. According to CORS specification, if you set this to true , you cannot use * for other CORS attributes.
route.allow_origins_by_regex: Regex to match origins that allow CORS. For example, [".*\.test.com$"] can match all subdomains of test.com . When configured, only domains matching the RegEx will be allowed and allow_origins will be ignored.
route.allow_origins_by_metadata: Origins to enable CORS referenced from allow_origins set in the Plugin metadata. For example, if "allow_origins": {"EXAMPLE": "https://example.com"} is set in the Plugin metadata, then ["EXAMPLE"] can be used to allow CORS on the origin https://example.com .
route.timing_allow_origins: Comma-separated string of origins to allow access to the resource timing information. See Timing-Allow-Origin for more details.
route.timing_allow_origins_by_regex: Regex to match origins for enabling access to the resource timing information. For example, [".*\.test.com"] can match all subdomains of test.com . When configured, only domains matching the RegEx will be allowed and timing_allow_origins will be ignored.

overview: The uri-blocker Plugin intercepts user requests with a set of block_rules .

route.block_rules: List of regex filter rules. If the request URI hits any one of the rules, the response code is set to the rejected_code and the user request is terminated. For example, ["root.exe", "root.m+"] .
route.rejected_code: HTTP status code returned when the request URI hits any of the block_rules .
route.rejected_msg: HTTP response body returned when the request URI hits any of the block_rules .
route.case_insensitive: When set to true , ignores the case when matching request URI.

overview: The ip-restriction Plugin supports restricting access to Upstream resources by IP addresses, through either configuring a whitelist or blacklist of IP addresses. Restricting IP to resources helps prevent unauthorized access and harden API security.

route.whitelist: List of IPs or CIDR ranges to allow. Exactly one of whitelist or blacklist must be configured.
route.blacklist: List of IPs or CIDR ranges to deny. Exactly one of whitelist or blacklist must be configured.
route.message: Message returned to the client when the IP is blocked.
route.response_code: HTTP response code returned when the request is rejected due to IP address restriction.

overview: The ua-restriction Plugin supports restricting access to upstream resources through either configuring an allowlist or denylist of user agents. A common use case is to prevent web crawlers from overloading the upstream resources and causing service degradation.

route.bypass_missing: If true , bypasses the UA restriction check when the User-Agent header is missing.
route.allowlist: List of allowed user agents (supports regex). Exactly one of allowlist or denylist must be configured.
route.denylist: List of denied user agents (supports regex). Exactly one of allowlist or denylist must be configured.
route.message: Message returned to the client when the user agent is not allowed.

examples.title: Reject Web Crawlers and Customize Error Message

overview: The referer-restriction Plugin can be used to restrict access to a Service or a Route by whitelisting/blacklisting the Referer request header.

route.whitelist: List of hostnames to whitelist. A hostname can start with * for wildcard.
route.blacklist: List of hostnames to blacklist. A hostname can start with * for wildcard.
route.message: Message returned when access is not allowed.
route.bypass_missing: When set to true , bypasses the check when the Referer request header is missing or malformed.

overview: The consumer-restriction Plugin enables access controls based on Consumer name, Route ID, Service ID, or Consumer Group ID.
The Plugin needs to work with authentication plugins, such as key-auth and jwt-auth , which means you should always create at least one Consumer in your use case. See examples below for more details.

route.type: Basis for restriction. Determines what value is checked against the allowlist or denylist.
route.whitelist: List of allowed values. At least one of whitelist , blacklist , or allowed_by_methods must be configured.
route.blacklist: List of denied values. At least one of whitelist , blacklist , or allowed_by_methods must be configured.
route.allowed_by_methods: List of objects specifying allowed HTTP methods per Consumer. At least one of whitelist , blacklist , or allowed_by_methods must be configured.
route.allowed_by_methods[].methods: List of HTTP methods allowed for the Consumer.
route.rejected_code: HTTP status code returned when the request is rejected.
route.rejected_msg: Message returned to the client when the request is rejected.

examples.title: Restrict Access by Consumers and HTTP Methods

overview: The csrf Plugin can be used to protect your API against CSRF attacks using the Double Submit Cookie method.

This Plugin considers the GET , HEAD and OPTIONS methods to be safe operations ( safe-methods ) and such requests are not checked for interception by an attacker. Other methods are termed as unsafe-methods .

route.name: Name of the token in the generated cookie.
route.expires: Expiration time in seconds of the CSRF cookie. Set to 0 to skip checking expiration time.
route.key: Secret key used to encrypt the cookie.

overview: The chaitin-waf Plugin integrates with the Chaitin WAF (SafeLine) service to provide advanced detection and prevention of web-based threats, enhancing application security and protecting sensitive user data.

route.mode: Mode to determine how the Plugin behaves for matched requests. In off mode, WAF checks are skipped. In monitor mode, requests with potential threats are logged but not blocked. In block mode, requests with threats are blocked as determined by the WAF service.
route.match: An array of matching rules. The Plugin uses these rules to decide whether to perform a WAF check on a request. If the list is empty, all requests are processed.
route.match.vars: An array of one or more matching conditions in the form of lua-resty-expr to conditionally execute the plugin.
route.append_waf_resp_header: If true, add response headers X-APISIX-CHAITIN-WAF , X-APISIX-CHAITIN-WAF-TIME , X-APISIX-CHAITIN-WAF-ACTION , and X-APISIX-CHAITIN-WAF-STATUS .
route.append_waf_debug_header: If true, add debugging headers X-APISIX-CHAITIN-WAF-ERROR and X-APISIX-CHAITIN-WAF-SERVER to the response. Effective only when append_waf_resp_header is true .
route.config: Chaitin WAF service configurations. These settings override the corresponding metadata defaults when specified.
route.config.connect_timeout: The connection timeout to the WAF service, in milliseconds.
route.config.send_timeout: The sending timeout for transmitting data to the WAF service, in milliseconds.
route.config.read_timeout: The reading timeout for receiving data from the WAF service, in milliseconds.
route.config.req_body_size: The maximum allowed request body size, in KB.
route.config.keepalive_size: The maximum number of idle connections to the WAF detection service that can be maintained concurrently.
route.config.keepalive_timeout: The idle connection timeout for the WAF service, in milliseconds.
route.config.real_client_ip: If true, the Plugin sends APISIX’s resolved client IP to the WAF service (the same value used elsewhere in APISIX, derived from the connection and apisix.trusted_addresses ). If false, the Plugin sends the IP of the peer directly connected to APISIX.
route.config.log_resp: If true, the Plugin also reports the response to the WAF service. See Response Logging .
route.config.resp_body_size: The amount of the response body to report, in KB. Set to 0 to report only the status line and response headers. Effective only when config.log_resp is true .
route.config.extra_ignored_content_types: A comma separated list of response Content-Type values to skip, in addition to the built-in ignored list. Effective only when config.log_resp is true .

examples.title: Block Malicious Requests on a Route

overview: The oas-validator Plugin validates incoming HTTP requests against an OpenAPI Specification (OAS) 3.x document before forwarding them to the upstream service. It can validate the request method, path, query parameters, request headers, and body.

The OpenAPI spec can be provided as an inline JSON string or fetched from a remote URL with configurable caching. Validation failures return a configurable HTTP error status, and detailed error messages can optionally be included in the response body.

route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered into memory. Requests with a larger body are rejected.
route.spec: Inline OpenAPI 3.x specification in JSON format. Required if spec_url is not set.
route.spec_url: URL to fetch the OpenAPI specification from. Required if spec is not set.
route.spec_url_request_headers: Custom HTTP request headers sent when fetching spec_url . Useful for authenticated specification endpoints.
route.ssl_verify: Whether to verify the TLS certificate when fetching spec_url .
route.timeout: HTTP request timeout in milliseconds for fetching spec_url .
route.verbose_errors: When true , include detailed validation error messages in the response body.
route.skip_request_body_validation: Skip validation of the request body.
route.skip_query_param_validation: Skip validation of query string parameters.
route.reject_if_not_match: When true , reject requests that fail validation. When false , log the validation failure and allow the request through.
route.rejection_status_code: HTTP status code to return when a request fails validation.

examples.title: Validate Requests with an Inline Specification
Validate Requests with a Remote Specification URL

overview: The ocsp-stapling Plugin dynamically sets the behavior of OCSP stapling in Nginx.

route.enabled: Like the ssl_stapling directive, enables or disables OCSP stapling feature.
route.skip_verify: Like the ssl_stapling_verify directive, enables or disables verification of OCSP responses.
route.cache_ttl: Specifies the expired time of OCSP response cache.

overview: The public-api Plugin exposes an internal API endpoint, making it publicly accessible. One of the primary use cases of this Plugin is to expose internal endpoints created by other Plugins.

route.uri: Internal endpoint to expose. If not configured, expose the Route URI.

examples.title: Expose Prometheus Metrics at Custom Endpoint

overview: The ai-proxy Plugin simplifies access to LLM and embedding models by transforming Plugin configurations into the designated request format. It supports the integration with OpenAI, DeepSeek, Azure, AIMLAPI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Gemini, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs.

In addition, the Plugin also supports logging LLM request information in the access log, such as token usage, model, time to the first response, and more. These log entries are also consumed by logging plugins such as http-logger and kafka-logger . These options do not affect error.log .

route.messages.role: Role of the message ( system , user , assistant ).
route.system: Optional system prompt blocks (e.g., [{"text": "You are a helpful assistant."}] ).
route.inferenceConfig: Optional inference parameters such as maxTokens , temperature , topP , etc.
route.stream: When true , the Plugin proxies the request to Bedrock’s ConverseStream endpoint and forwards the response in AWS EventStream ( application/vnd.amazon.eventstream ) binary framing. The flag is consumed by the Plugin and is not forwarded to Bedrock.
route.provider: LLM service provider. When set to openai , the Plugin will proxy the request to https://api.openai.com/chat/completions . When set to deepseek , the Plugin will proxy the request to https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions . When set to aimlapi , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to https://api.aimlapi.com/v1/chat/completions by default. When set to anthropic , the Plugin will proxy the request to https://api.anthropic.com/v1/chat/completions by default. When set to openrouter , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions by default. When set to gemini , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/chat/completions by default. When set to vertex-ai , the Plugin will proxy the request to https://aiplatform.googleapis.com by default and requires provider_conf or override . When set to bedrock , the Plugin will proxy the request to the AWS Bedrock Converse API ( https://bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com ) and signs the request with AWS SigV4. When set to openai-compatible , the Plugin will proxy the request to the custom endpoint configured in override .
route.provider_conf: Configuration for the specific provider. Required when provider is set to vertex-ai and override is not configured. Required when provider is set to bedrock .
route.provider_conf.region: When provider is vertex-ai , this is the Google Cloud Region. When provider is bedrock , this is the AWS region used to construct the Bedrock endpoint and to sign the request with SigV4 (required, must be non-empty).
route.auth.header: Authentication headers. At least one of header or query must be configured.
route.auth.query: Authentication query parameters. At least one of header or query must be configured.
route.auth.gcp: Configuration for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) authentication.
route.auth.gcp.service_account_json: Content of the GCP service account JSON file. This can also be configured by setting the GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT environment variable.
route.auth.gcp.max_ttl: Maximum TTL (in seconds) for caching the GCP access token.
route.auth.gcp.expire_early_secs: Seconds to expire the access token before its actual expiration time to avoid edge cases.
route.auth.aws: Configuration for AWS authentication. Required when provider is bedrock .
route.auth.aws.access_key_id: AWS access key ID used for SigV4 signing.
route.auth.aws.secret_access_key: AWS secret access key used for SigV4 signing. Stored encrypted.
route.auth.aws.session_token: Optional AWS session token for temporary credentials (e.g., from STS or assumed roles). Stored encrypted.
route.options: Model configurations. In addition to model , you can configure additional parameters and they will be forwarded to the upstream LLM service in the request body. For instance, if you are working with OpenAI, you can configure additional parameters such as temperature , top_p , and stream . See your LLM provider’s API documentation for more available options.
route.options.model: Name of the LLM model, such as gpt-4 or gpt-3.5 . Refer to the LLM provider’s API documentation for available models. When provider is bedrock and override.endpoint is not configured, model is required and may be a foundation model ID (e.g., anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0 ), a cross-region inference profile ID (e.g., us.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0 ), or an application inference profile ARN (e.g., arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:123456789012:application-inference-profile/abc123 ).
route.override.endpoint: Custom LLM provider endpoint, required when provider is openai-compatible . When provider is bedrock , this can be set to a custom Bedrock endpoint. If the override URL includes a path containing reserved characters (e.g., Bedrock inference profile ARNs containing : or / ), those characters MUST be URL-encoded ( : → %3A , / → %2F ) so the model ID is preserved as a single path segment.
route.override.llm_options: Provider-aware LLM options. See Provider-aware max_tokens mapping .
route.override.llm_options.max_tokens: Maximum number of output tokens. APISIX automatically maps this to the provider-specific field name (e.g. max_completion_tokens for OpenAI Chat Completions, max_output_tokens for OpenAI Responses API, max_tokens for most other providers). Always force-overwrites the client value.
route.override.request_body: Per target-protocol request body overrides. Keys are target protocol names ( openai-chat , openai-responses , openai-embeddings , anthropic-messages , bedrock-converse ); values are partial request bodies that are deep-merged into the outgoing body (objects merged recursively, arrays and scalars replaced wholesale). See Per-protocol request body override .
route.override.request_body_force_override: When false (default), client request body fields take priority and override.request_body values only fill in missing fields. When true , override.request_body values forcefully overwrite client fields. Does not affect override.llm_options , which always force-overwrites.
route.logging: Logging configurations. Does not affect error.log .
route.logging.summaries: If true, logs request LLM model, duration, request, and response tokens.
route.logging.payloads: If true, logs request and response payload.
route.timeout: Request timeout in milliseconds when requesting the LLM service. Applied per socket operation (connect / send / read block); does not cap the total duration of a streaming response.
route.max_stream_duration_ms: Maximum wall-clock duration (in milliseconds) for a streaming AI response. If the upstream keeps sending data past this deadline, the gateway closes the connection. Unset means no cap. Use this to protect the gateway from upstream bugs that produce tokens indefinitely. When the limit is hit mid-stream, the downstream SSE stream is truncated (no protocol-specific terminator such as [DONE] , message_stop , or response.completed ); well-behaved clients should treat a missing terminator as an incomplete response.
route.max_response_bytes: Maximum total bytes read from the upstream for a single AI response (streaming or non-streaming). If exceeded, the gateway closes the connection. For non-streaming responses with Content-Length , the check is performed before reading the body; for chunked (no- Content-Length ) non-streaming responses and for streaming responses, the cap is enforced incrementally as bytes are received. Unset means no cap.
route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes that the plugin reads into memory. Requests whose body exceeds this limit are rejected with 413 . Prevents unbounded memory buffering of large request bodies.
route.keepalive: If true, keeps the connection alive when requesting the LLM service.
route.keepalive_timeout: Keepalive timeout in milliseconds when connecting to the LLM service.
route.keepalive_pool: Keepalive pool size for the LLM service connection.
route.ssl_verify: If true, verifies the LLM service’s certificate.
route.streaming_flush_interval_ms: Interval in milliseconds for the background flush thread. When > 0 (default: 10 ), a background timer calls ngx.flush(false) every N ms, batching output for bursty upstreams. For SSE streams, only complete frames or converted events queued for the client trigger a flush; partial frames wait for the remaining upstream data. If a periodic flush returns nothing to flush , the stream continues. When 0 , the background thread is disabled and each chunk is flushed synchronously via ngx.flush(true) , guaranteeing immediate client delivery.

overview: The ai-proxy-multi Plugin simplifies access to LLM and embedding models by transforming Plugin configurations into the designated request format for OpenAI, DeepSeek, Azure, AIMLAPI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Gemini, Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs. It extends the capabilities of ai-proxy with load balancing, retries, fallbacks, and health checks.

In addition, the Plugin also supports logging LLM request information in the access log, such as token usage, model, time to the first response, and more. These log entries are also consumed by logging plugins such as http-logger and kafka-logger , and do not affect error log.

route.messages.role: Role of the message ( system , user , assistant ).
route.system: Optional system prompt blocks (e.g., [{"text": "You are a helpful assistant."}] ).
route.inferenceConfig: Optional inference parameters such as maxTokens , temperature , topP , stopSequences , etc.
route.stream: When true , the Plugin proxies the request to Bedrock’s ConverseStream endpoint and forwards the response in AWS EventStream ( application/vnd.amazon.eventstream ) binary framing. The flag is consumed by the Plugin and is not forwarded to Bedrock.
route.fallback_strategy: Fallback strategy. When set, the Plugin will check whether the specified instance’s token has been exhausted when a request is forwarded. If so, forward the request to the next instance regardless of the instance priority. When not set, the Plugin will not forward the request to low priority instances when token of the high priority instance is exhausted.
route.fallback_http_statuses: Additional upstream HTTP status codes that make the request fall back to another instance, on top of the http_429 and http_5xx entries of fallback_strategy . Use it for statuses that mean the instance’s credential is unusable rather than the request being wrong, such as [401, 402] when an API key is expired or out of quota. It is opt-in per status because most 4xx responses are caused by the request itself and retrying them on another instance would only burn quota. max_retries and retry_on_failure_within_ms bound these retries the same way they bound the fallback_strategy ones.
route.max_retries: Maximum number of fallback retries after the initial request fails. Bounds how many additional instances a single request tries, so it does not exhaust every configured instance. Only takes effect together with fallback_strategy or fallback_http_statuses . When unset, the Plugin retries until an instance succeeds or all are tried.
route.retry_on_failure_within_ms: Only fall back to another instance when the upstream fails within this many milliseconds. Fast failures (such as connection errors or quick 429 / 5xx ) are retried, while a slow failure that takes longer than this is returned to the client directly to avoid doubling the wait time. Only takes effect together with fallback_strategy or fallback_http_statuses . When unset, the Plugin retries regardless of how long the failed attempt took.
route.balancer.algorithm: Load balancing algorithm. When set to roundrobin , weighted round robin algorithm is used. When set to chash , consistent hashing algorithm is used. When set to semantic , the Plugin picks an instance by the semantic similarity between the request prompt and each instance’s examples , and its options are configured under semantic_opts . Note that semantic does not participate in health checks or fallback_strategy / retry — an upstream failure on the chosen instance is returned to the client; it only falls back (to the semantic_opts.fallback instance, else the first instance) when no instance clears its threshold or embedding fails.
route.balancer.hash_on: Used when type is chash . Support hashing on NGINX variables , headers, cookie, consumer, or a combination of NGINX variables .
route.balancer.key: Used when type is chash . When hash_on is set to header or cookie , key is required. When hash_on is set to consumer , key is not required as the consumer name will be used as the key automatically.
route.instances.name: Name of the LLM service instance. It must be unique within instances , since it identifies the instance in the balancer, in its health checker, and in other Plugins that reference it, such as ai-rate-limiting .
route.instances.provider: LLM service provider. When set to openai , the Plugin will proxy the request to api.openai.com . When set to deepseek , the Plugin will proxy the request to api.deepseek.com . When set to aimlapi , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to api.aimlapi.com by default. When set to anthropic , the Plugin will proxy the request to api.anthropic.com by default. When set to openrouter , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to openrouter.ai by default. When set to gemini , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to generativelanguage.googleapis.com by default. When set to vertex-ai , the Plugin will proxy the request to aiplatform.googleapis.com by default and requires provider_conf or override . When set to bedrock , the Plugin proxies the request to Amazon Bedrock’s Converse API at bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com and signs the request with AWS SigV4. Requires provider_conf.region and auth.aws . When set to openai-compatible , the Plugin will proxy the request to the custom endpoint configured in override .
route.instances.provider_conf: Configuration for the specific provider. Required when provider is set to vertex-ai and override is not configured. Required when provider is set to bedrock .
route.instances.provider_conf.region: When provider is vertex-ai , this is the Google Cloud Region. When provider is bedrock , this is the AWS region used to construct the Bedrock endpoint and to sign the request with SigV4 (required, must be non-empty).
route.instances.priority: Priority of the LLM instance in load balancing. priority takes precedence over weight .
route.instances.weight: Weight of the LLM instance in load balancing.
route.instances.auth.header: Authentication headers. At least one of the header and query should be configured.
route.instances.auth.query: Authentication query parameters. At least one of the header and query should be configured.
route.instances.auth.gcp: Configuration for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) authentication.
route.instances.auth.gcp.service_account_json: Content of the GCP service account JSON file. This can also be configured by setting the GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT environment variable.
route.instances.auth.gcp.max_ttl: Maximum TTL (in seconds) for caching the GCP access token.
route.instances.auth.gcp.expire_early_secs: Seconds to expire the access token before its actual expiration time to avoid edge cases.
route.instances.auth.aws: AWS IAM credentials for SigV4 signing (Bedrock). Required when provider is bedrock .
route.instances.auth.aws.secret_access_key: AWS IAM secret access key. Encrypted at rest.
route.instances.auth.aws.session_token: AWS session token for temporary credentials (e.g., from STS assume-role). Encrypted at rest.
route.instances.options: Model configurations. In addition to model , you can configure additional parameters and they will be forwarded to the upstream LLM service in the request body. For instance, if you are working with OpenAI, DeepSeek, or AIMLAPI, you can configure additional parameters such as max_tokens , temperature , top_p , and stream . See your LLM provider’s API documentation for more available options.
route.instances.options.model: Name of the LLM model, such as gpt-4 or gpt-3.5 . See your LLM provider’s API documentation for more available models. For Bedrock, this can be a foundation model ID (e.g., anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0 ), a cross-region inference profile ID (e.g., us.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0 ), or an application inference profile ARN (e.g., arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:123456789012:application-inference-profile/abc123 ).
route.instances.examples: Used when algorithm is semantic . Example utterances representing this instance’s intent; each is embedded into its own reference vector. Required for every instance when algorithm is semantic , including the one named by semantic_opts.fallback .
route.instances.threshold: Used when algorithm is semantic . Per-instance minimum cosine similarity; overrides semantic_opts.threshold .
route.logging.summaries: If true, log request LLM model, duration, request, and response tokens.
route.logging.payloads: If true, log request and response payload.
route.instances.override.endpoint: LLM provider endpoint to replace the default endpoint with. If not configured, the Plugin uses the default OpenAI endpoint https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions . When provider is bedrock , this can be set to a custom Bedrock endpoint. If the override URL includes a path containing reserved characters (e.g., Bedrock inference profile ARNs containing : or / ), those characters MUST be URL-encoded ( : → %3A , / → %2F ) so the model ID is preserved as a single path segment.
route.instances.override.llm_options: Provider-aware LLM options. See Provider-aware max_tokens mapping in the ai-proxy documentation.
route.instances.override.llm_options.max_token: Maximum number of output tokens. APISIX automatically maps this to the provider-specific field name. Always force-overwrites the client value.
route.instances.override.request_body: Per target-protocol request body overrides. See Per-protocol request body override in the ai-proxy documentation.
route.instances.override.request_body_force_ov: When false (default), client request body fields take priority and instances.override.request_body values only fill in missing fields. When true , instances.override.request_body values forcefully overwrite client fields. Does not affect instances.override.llm_options .
route.instances.checks: Health check configurations. Note that at the moment, OpenAI, DeepSeek, and AIMLAPI do not provide an official health check endpoint. Other LLM services that you can configure under openai-compatible provider may have available health check endpoints.
route.instances.checks.active.concurrency: Number of upstream nodes to be checked at the same time.
route.instances.checks.active.https_verify_cer: If true, verify the node’s TLS certificate.
route.instances.checks.active.healthy.interval: Time interval of checking healthy nodes, in seconds.
route.instances.checks.active.healthy.http_sta: An array of HTTP status codes that defines a healthy node.
route.instances.checks.active.healthy.successe: Number of successful probes to define a healthy node.
route.instances.checks.active.unhealthy.interv: Time interval of checking unhealthy nodes, in seconds.
route.instances.checks.active.unhealthy.http_s: An array of HTTP status codes that defines an unhealthy node.
route.instances.checks.active.unhealthy.http_f: Number of HTTP failures to define an unhealthy node.
route.instances.checks.active.unhealthy.timeou: Number of probe timeouts to define an unhealthy node.
route.semantic_opts: Options for the semantic balancer, grouped in one place. Required when balancer.algorithm is semantic .
route.semantic_opts.threshold: Global minimum cosine similarity an instance must reach to be selected. The default of 0 admits essentially any prompt (real embeddings are rarely dissimilar enough to score below 0), so the fallback only ever runs if you raise this above 0. When no instance clears its threshold, the request falls back to the fallback instance, or the first instance if none is named.
route.semantic_opts.fallback: Name of the instance to route to when no instance clears its threshold or the embedding request fails. It is otherwise a normal ranked instance and needs examples like the rest. Defaults to the first instance when unset.
route.semantic_opts.debugging: If true, expose per-instance scores and the routing decision via X-AI-Semantic-Scores and X-AI-Semantic-Picked-Instance response headers, for debugging.
route.semantic_opts.embeddings: Embedding service configuration used to score prompts against each instance’s examples .
route.semantic_opts.embeddings.provider: Embedding provider used by the semantic algorithm.
route.semantic_opts.embeddings.endpoint: Embedding API endpoint. Optional for openai (defaults to the public API). Required for azure-openai , where it must be the full URL including the deployment path and API version, e.g. https://{resource}.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/{deployment}/embeddings?api-version=2024-02-01 .
route.semantic_opts.embeddings.auth: Authentication configurations for the embedding service.
route.semantic_opts.embeddings.auth.query: Authentication query parameters. Encrypted at rest.
route.semantic_opts.embeddings.timeout: Embedding request timeout in milliseconds. The query prompt is embedded synchronously on every request, so this bounds the latency added to each request when the embedding endpoint is slow or down (the request then fails open to the fallback).
route.semantic_opts.embeddings.ssl_verify: If true, verify the embedding service’s certificate.
route.timeout: Request timeout in milliseconds when requesting the LLM service. Applied per socket operation (connect / send / read block); does not cap the total duration of a streaming response.
route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes that the plugin reads into memory. Requests whose body exceeds this limit are rejected with 413 . Prevents unbounded memory buffering of large request bodies.
route.max_stream_duration_ms: Maximum wall-clock duration (in milliseconds) for a streaming AI response. If the upstream keeps sending data past this deadline, the gateway closes the connection. Unset means no cap. Use this to protect the gateway from upstream bugs that produce tokens indefinitely. When the limit is hit mid-stream, the downstream SSE stream is truncated (no protocol-specific terminator such as [DONE] , message_stop , or response.completed ); well-behaved clients should treat a missing terminator as an incomplete response.
route.max_response_bytes: Maximum total bytes read from the upstream for a single AI response (streaming or non-streaming). If exceeded, the gateway closes the connection. For non-streaming responses with Content-Length , the check is performed before reading the body; for chunked (no- Content-Length ) non-streaming responses and for streaming responses, the cap is enforced incrementally as bytes are received. Unset means no cap.
route.keepalive: If true, keep the connection alive when requesting the LLM service.
route.keepalive_timeout: Request timeout in milliseconds when requesting the LLM service.
route.keepalive_pool: Keepalive pool size for when connecting with the LLM service.
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify the LLM service’s certificate.

overview: The ai-request-rewrite Plugin processes client requests by forwarding them to LLM services for transformation before relaying them to Upstream services. This enables LLM-powered modifications such as data redaction, content enrichment, or reformatting. The Plugin supports integration with OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, Vertex AI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, and other OpenAI-compatible APIs.

route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered into memory. Requests with a larger body are rejected.
route.prompt: The prompt to send to the LLM service for rewriting the client request.
route.provider: LLM service provider. When set to aimlapi , the Plugin uses the OpenAI-compatible driver and proxies the request to https://api.aimlapi.com/v1/chat/completions . When set to openai-compatible , the Plugin proxies requests to the custom endpoint configured in override . When set to azure-openai , the Plugin also proxies requests to the custom endpoint configured in override and additionally omits the model parameter from the request body sent to Azure OpenAI.
route.auth.header: Authentication headers. Key must match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ . At least one of header and query should be configured.
route.auth.query: Authentication query parameters. Key must match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$ . At least one of header and query should be configured.
route.options: Model configurations. In addition to model , you can configure additional parameters and they will be forwarded to the upstream LLM service in the request body. For instance, if you are working with OpenAI, you can configure additional parameters such as temperature , top_p , and stream . See your LLM provider’s API documentation for more available options.
route.options.model: Name of the LLM model, such as gpt-4 or gpt-3.5 . See your LLM provider’s API documentation for more available models.
route.override.endpoint: LLM provider endpoint. Required when provider is openai-compatible .
route.timeout: Request timeout in milliseconds when requesting the LLM service.
route.keepalive: If true, keep the connection alive when requesting the LLM service.
route.keepalive_timeout: Keepalive timeout in milliseconds for requests to the LLM service.
route.keepalive_pool: Keepalive pool size for connections to the LLM service.
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify the LLM service’s SSL certificate.

overview: The ai-rate-limiting Plugin enforces token-based rate limiting for requests sent to LLM services. It helps manage API usage by controlling the number of tokens consumed within a specified time frame, ensuring fair resource allocation and preventing excessive load on the service. It is often used with ai-proxy or ai-proxy-multi Plugin.

route.limit: The maximum number of tokens allowed within a given time interval. At least one of limit and instances.limit should be configured. Required if rules is not configured.
route.time_window: The time interval corresponding to the rate limiting limit in seconds. At least one of time_window and instances.time_window should be configured. Required if rules is not configured.
route.show_limit_quota_header: If true, includes rate limiting response headers. When rules is not set, the headers are X-AI-RateLimit-Limit-* , X-AI-RateLimit-Remaining-* , and X-AI-RateLimit-Reset-* , where * is the instance name. When rules is set, see rules.header_prefix for details.
route.limit_strategy: Type of token to apply rate limiting. total_tokens is the sum of prompt_tokens and completion_tokens . When set to expression , the cost_expr field is used to dynamically calculate token cost.
route.cost_expr: Lua arithmetic expression for dynamic token cost calculation. Variables are injected from the LLM API raw usage response fields. Missing variables default to 0. Only valid when limit_strategy is expression . Example: input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + output_tokens .
route.instances.name: Name of the LLM service instance.
route.instances.limit: The maximum number of tokens allowed within a given time interval for an instance.
route.instances.time_window: The time interval corresponding to the rate limiting limit in seconds for an instance.
route.rejected_code: The HTTP status code returned when a request exceeding the quota is rejected.
route.rejected_msg: The response body returned when a request exceeding the quota is rejected.
route.policy: The policy for the rate limiting counter. If it is local , the counter is stored in local memory. If it is redis , the counter is stored on a Redis instance. If it is redis-cluster , the counter is stored in a Redis cluster. If it is redis-sentinel , the counter is stored on the Redis master discovered through Sentinel. Use a Redis-based policy to share token counters across gateway nodes in a distributed deployment.
route.allow_degradation: If true, allow APISIX to continue serving requests without the Plugin when the Redis backend is unavailable.
route.redis_host: The address of the Redis node. Required when policy is redis .
route.redis_port: The port of the Redis node when policy is redis .
route.redis_username: The username for Redis if Redis ACL is used. If you use the legacy authentication method requirepass , configure only the redis_password . Used when policy is redis or redis-sentinel .
route.redis_password: The password of the Redis node when policy is redis , redis-cluster , or redis-sentinel .
route.redis_database: The database number in Redis when policy is redis or redis-sentinel .
route.redis_timeout: The Redis timeout value in milliseconds when policy is redis or redis-cluster .
route.redis_ssl: If true, use SSL to connect to Redis when policy is redis .
route.redis_ssl_verify: If true, verify the server SSL certificate when policy is redis .
route.redis_server_name: TLS SNI when policy is redis and redis_ssl is true. Defaults to redis_host . When redis_ssl_verify is true the certificate must also match this name, so set it when redis_host is an alias the certificate does not cover.
route.redis_cluster_nodes: The list of Redis cluster nodes with at least one address. Required when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_name: The name of the Redis cluster. Required when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_ssl: If true, use SSL to connect to Redis when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_ssl_verify: If true, verify the server SSL certificate when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_sentinels: The list of Sentinel nodes. Required when policy is redis-sentinel . Each item must contain host and port .
route.redis_master_name: The Redis master name monitored by Sentinel. Required when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.sentinel_username: The username for Sentinel when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.sentinel_password: The password for Sentinel when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.redis_role: The Redis role selected through Sentinel when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.redis_connect_timeout: The Redis connection timeout in milliseconds when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.redis_read_timeout: The Redis read timeout in milliseconds when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.redis_keepalive_timeout: The Redis keepalive timeout in milliseconds when policy is redis-sentinel .
route.rules: An array of rate-limiting rules that are applied sequentially. If configured, this takes precedence over limit and time_window .
route.rules.count: The maximum number of tokens allowed within a given time interval. Can be a static integer or a variable expression like $http_custom_limit .
route.rules.time_window: The time interval corresponding to the rate limiting count in seconds. Can be a static integer or a variable expression.
route.rules.key: The key to count requests by. If the configured key does not exist, the rule will not be executed. The key is interpreted as a combination of variables. All variables should be prefixed by dollar signs ( $ ). For example, $http_custom_a $http_custom_b .
route.rules.header_prefix: Prefix for rate limiting response headers. When configured, the prefix is inserted after X-AI- in the header name. For example, with header_prefix set to test , the headers become X-AI-Test-RateLimit-Limit , X-AI-Test-RateLimit-Remaining , and X-AI-Test-RateLimit-Reset . When not configured, the index of the rule in the rules array is used as the prefix. For example, headers for the first rule will be X-AI-1-RateLimit-Limit , X-AI-1-RateLimit-Remaining , and X-AI-1-RateLimit-Reset .

overview: The ai-prompt-decorator Plugin modifies user input prompts by prefixing and appending pre-engineered prompts to set contexts in content generation. This practice helps the model operate within desired guidelines during interactions.

route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered into memory. Requests with a larger body are rejected.
route.prepend: An array of prompt objects to be prepended.
route.append: An array of prompt objects to be appended.

overview: The ai-prompt-template Plugin supports pre-configuring prompt templates that only accept user inputs in designated template variables, in a “fill in the blank” fashion. It simplifies access to LLM providers, such as OpenAI and Anthropic, by letting you define reusable prompt structures.

route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered into memory. Requests with a larger body are rejected.
route.templates.name: Name of the template. When requesting the Route, the request should include the template name that corresponds to the configured template.
route.templates.template.model: Name of the LLM model, such as gpt-4 or gpt-3.5 . See your LLM provider API documentation for more available models.
route.templates.template.messages.content: Content of the message (prompt). Use {{variable_name}} syntax to define template variables that will be filled from the request body.

overview: The ai-prompt-guard Plugin safeguards your LLM endpoints by inspecting and validating incoming prompt messages. It checks the content of requests against user-defined allowed and denied patterns to ensure that only approved inputs are forwarded to the upstream LLM. Based on its configuration, the Plugin can either examine just the latest message or the entire conversation history, and it can be set to check prompts from all roles or only from end users.

When both allow_patterns and deny_patterns are configured, the Plugin first ensures that at least one allow_patterns is matched. If none match, the request is rejected. If an allowed pattern is matched, it then checks for any occurrences of denied patterns.

route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered into memory. Requests with a larger body are rejected.
route.match_all_roles: If true , validate messages from all roles. If false , validate the message from user role only.
route.match_all_conversation_history: If true , concatenate and check all messages in the conversation history. If false , only check the content of the last message.
route.allow_patterns: An array of regex patterns that messages should match. When configured, messages must match at least one pattern to be considered valid.
route.deny_patterns: An array of regex patterns that messages should not match. If messages match any of the patterns, the request is rejected. If both allow_patterns and deny_patterns are configured, the Plugin first ensures that at least one allow_patterns is matched.
route.fail_mode: Behavior when the request body matches no recognized AI protocol that this plugin can inspect (for example, plain HTTP traffic on a Consumer-bound plugin, or a request that did not pass through ai-proxy ). skip : let the request pass through unchecked; warn : pass through and log a warning; error : reject the request.
