overview: The ai-aws-content-moderation Plugin integrates with AWS Comprehend to check content for toxicity when proxying to LLMs, such as profanity, hate speech, insult, harassment, violence, and more, rejecting requests if the evaluated outcome exceeds the configured threshold.

The Plugin is protocol-aware: it extracts the prompt content from the LLM request (for example messages[].content ) and moderates only that decoded text, rather than the raw request body. request_check_roles selects which message roles are moderated, and request_check_mode can narrow user / tool moderation to the newest turn so conversation history is not re-scored on every request.

route.comprehend.endpoint: AWS Comprehend service endpoint. If not specified, it defaults to https://comprehend.{region}.amazonaws.com . If set, it must match the pattern ^https?:// .
route.comprehend.ssl_verify: If true, enable TLS certificate verification.
route.moderation_categories: Key-value pairs of moderation category and their corresponding threshold. In each pair, the key should be one of PROFANITY , HATE_SPEECH , INSULT , HARASSMENT_OR_ABUSE , SEXUAL , or VIOLENCE_OR_THREAT ; and the threshold value should be between 0 and 1 (inclusive).
route.moderation_threshold: Overall toxicity threshold. A higher value means more toxic content allowed. This option differs from the individual category thresholds in moderation_categories . For example, if moderation_categories is set with a PROFANITY threshold of 0.5 , and a request has a PROFANITY score of 0.1 , the request will not exceed the category threshold. However, if the request has other categories like SEXUAL or VIOLENCE_OR_THREAT exceeding the moderation_threshold , the request will be rejected.
route.check_request: If true , moderate the request content.
route.check_response: If true , moderate the LLM response content.
route.request_check_roles: Which message roles to moderate on the request side. user , tool and assistant follow request_check_mode ; system is checked on every request (it can be poisoned by malicious ToolCall arguments overwriting the system prompt) and also covers OpenAI’s developer role, which replaces system on newer models. assistant messages in a request are client-supplied history rather than the model’s own output, so they are moderated by default as well. Note: tool-result moderation applies to OpenAI-compatible formats where the tool output is a distinct tool role/item; for Anthropic and Bedrock (tool results are nested blocks inside user messages) tool content is not extracted.
route.request_check_mode: Which user/tool/assistant messages to moderate. last : only the latest consecutive block of selected-role messages (the newest turn). all : every selected-role message. Does not apply to system , which is always moderated when enabled via request_check_roles . Note that last combined with assistant widens the block rather than narrowing it, because assistant turns no longer end it — drop assistant from request_check_roles to moderate only the newest turn.
route.request_check_length_limit: Maximum bytes of request content per Comprehend text segment. Longer content is split on character boundaries into several segments, which are then batched into as few Comprehend calls as possible. The upper bound is AWS Comprehend’s 1 KB per-segment limit.
route.response_check_length_limit: Maximum bytes of response content per Comprehend text segment. Longer content is split on character boundaries into several segments, which are then batched into as few Comprehend calls as possible. The upper bound is AWS Comprehend’s 1 KB per-segment limit.
route.stream_check_mode: Streaming moderation mode, used when check_response is true . realtime : moderate batches while the response streams, replacing the rest of the stream once a batch is flagged. final_packet : moderate the assembled response and annotate the last chunk with risk_level .
route.stream_check_cache_size: Maximum characters per moderation batch in realtime mode.
route.stream_check_interval: Seconds between batch checks in realtime mode.
route.deny_code: HTTP status code returned when a request is rejected. Defaults to 200 so the provider-compatible refusal parses as a normal completion in client SDKs; set a 4xx to surface denies as HTTP errors instead. Streaming responses denied mid-stream keep the status already sent to the client.
route.deny_message: Message returned when a request or response is rejected. If unset, the moderation reason (for example request body exceeds toxicity threshold ) is returned.
route.timeout: Comprehend request timeout in milliseconds.
route.keepalive: If true , keep the Comprehend connection alive for reuse.
route.keepalive_timeout: Idle time in milliseconds before a pooled Comprehend connection is closed.
route.fail_mode: Behavior when the request did not pass through ai-proxy / ai-proxy-multi and therefore cannot be moderated as an AI request. skip : let the request pass through unchecked; warn : pass through and log a warning; error : reject the request.

overview: The ai-aliyun-content-moderation Plugin integrates with Aliyun Machine-Assisted Moderation Plus to check request and response content for risk level when proxying to LLMs, such as profanity, hate speech, insult, harassment, violence, and more, rejecting requests if the evaluated outcome exceeds the configured threshold.

Please ensure that the access_key_secret is correctly configured in the Plugin. If misconfigured, the moderation check will fail and the request may still be forwarded to the LLM Upstream. You will see a Specified signature is not matched with our calculation error in the gateway’s error log from the Plugin.

route.access_key_secret: Aliyun secret access key. The value is encrypted with AES before being stored in etcd.
route.check_request: If true , moderate the request content.
route.check_response: If true , moderate the response content.
route.stream_check_mode: Streaming moderation mode. realtime : batched checks during streaming. final_packet : append risk level at the end.
route.stream_check_cache_size: Maximum bytes per moderation batch in realtime mode. Length is measured using Lua string length, so for UTF-8 text non-ASCII characters may consume multiple bytes.
route.stream_check_interval: Seconds between batch checks in realtime mode.
route.request_check_roles: Which message roles to moderate on the request side. user and tool follow request_check_mode ; system is checked on every request (it can be poisoned by malicious ToolCall arguments overwriting the system prompt) and also covers OpenAI’s developer role, which replaces system on newer models. The default ["user"] preserves the previous behavior. Note: tool-result moderation applies to OpenAI-compatible formats where the tool output is a distinct tool role/item; for Anthropic and Bedrock (tool results are nested blocks inside user messages) tool content is not extracted.
route.request_check_mode: Which user/tool messages to moderate. last : only the latest consecutive block of selected-role messages (the newest turn). all : every selected-role message. Does not apply to system , which is always moderated when enabled via request_check_roles .
route.request_check_length_limit: Request content length limit. If exceeded, the content is sent to Aliyun in chunks. For instance, if the request content is 250 characters and request_check_length_limit is set to 100 , the content is sent in 3 requests to Aliyun.
route.response_check_length_limit: Response content length limit. If exceeded, the content is sent to Aliyun in chunks. For instance, if the response content is 250 characters and response_check_length_limit is set to 100 , the content is sent in 3 requests to Aliyun.
route.risk_level_bar: If the evaluated risk level is lower than the risk_level_bar , the request or response will be passed through to Upstream LLM or client respectively.
route.deny_code: Rejection HTTP status code. Defaults to 200 so the provider-compatible refusal parses as a normal completion in client SDKs; set a 4xx to surface denies as HTTP errors instead.
route.timeout: Timeout in milliseconds.
route.keepalive: If true , enable HTTP connection keepalive to Aliyun.
route.keepalive_pool: Maximum number of connections in the keepalive pool.
route.ssl_verify: If true , enable SSL certificate verification.
route.fail_mode: Behavior when the request is not a recognized AI request that this plugin can inspect (for example, plain HTTP traffic on a Consumer-bound plugin, or a request that did not pass through ai-proxy ). skip : let the request pass through unchecked; warn : pass through and log a warning; error : reject the request.

overview: The ai-rag Plugin implements the retrieval step of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) request flow. It generates an embedding from the request, performs a vector search, adds the retrieved content to the protocol-specific LLM request input, and removes the ai_rag request object before the request is proxied.

The current implementation supports Azure OpenAI for embeddings and Azure AI Search for vector search. Use the ai-proxy Plugin in the same request flow to proxy the augmented request to the LLM provider. The Plugin does not create or populate a search index; prepare the index and its content before sending requests through APISIX.

route.dimensions: The number of dimensions the resulting output embeddings should have. It should match the dimension of your embedding model. For instance, the dimensions for text-embedding-ada-002 are fixed at 1536. For text-embedding-3-small or text-embedding-3-large , dimensions range from 1 to 1536 and 3072, respectively.

route.apisix_etcd_modify_indexes: Number of changes to etcd by APISIX keys.

route.apisix_llm_completion_tokens: Total number of completion tokens generated by LLM requests.

route.apisix_llm_completion_tokens_dist: Distribution of completion tokens generated per LLM request.

route.apisix_ai_cache_misses_total: Total number of AI cache misses.
route.apisix_ai_cache_bypasses_total: Total number of requests that bypassed the AI cache.
route.apisix_ai_cache_embedding_latency: Latency of AI cache embedding calls in milliseconds.

route.apisix_shared_dict_capacity_bytes: The total capacity of an NGINX shared dictionary .

route.apisix_stream_connection_total: Total number of connections handled per Stream Route.

route.apisix_stream_status: Counted once per Stream session when it ends, classified by how it ended.
route.apisix_stream_bandwidth: Total bandwidth in bytes proxied by the Stream subsystem, per listening address and direction.

route.request_type: Request category: traditional_http , websocket , ai_chat , or ai_stream . A request answered with 101 Switching Protocols is websocket .
route.request_llm_model: Model name requested by the client.
route.llm_model: Effective target model for the AI request. Uses the model configured on the AI instance when present; otherwise uses the model requested by the client. Empty for traditional HTTP traffic.
route.response_source: Response origin: apisix for responses generated by APISIX, nginx for NGINX proxy errors, or upstream for responses received from the Upstream.

route.type: Direction relative to APISIX, matching apisix_bandwidth : ingress for bytes APISIX received, egress for bytes APISIX sent.
route.route_id: ID of the Route that the metric corresponds to when prefer_name is false (default), and name of the Route when prefer_name is true . Defaults to an empty string if a request does not match any Route.
route.service_id: ID of the Service that the metric corresponds to when prefer_name is false (default), and name of the Service when prefer_name is true . Defaults to an empty string if the matched Route does not belong to any Service.

route.include_method: If true, includes the HTTP method in metric tags.
route.constant_tags: Static key-value tags attached to all metrics generated by this Route. Useful for grouping metrics over certain signals.
route.batch_max_size: Maximum number of metric entries per batch. Once reached, the batch is sent to the Datadog agent. Set to 1 for immediate processing.
route.inactive_timeout: Maximum time in seconds to wait for new metric entries before sending the batch. The value should be smaller than buffer_duration .

route.request.latency: Time taken to process the request, in milliseconds.
route.upstream.latency: Time taken to proxy the request to the upstream server until a response is received, in milliseconds.

route.service_name: Name of the Service. If not present or if the attribute prefer_name is set to false, falls back to the Service ID.

route.response_status_class: HTTP response status code class, such as 2xx , 4xx , or 5xx . Available from APISIX version 3.14.0.

route.timeout: OpenFunction action and HTTP call timeout in ms.
route.keepalive: When set to true keeps the connection alive for reuse.
route.keepalive_timeout: Time is ms for connection to remain idle without closing.
route.keepalive_pool: Maximum number of requests that can be sent on this connection before closing it.

overview: The dubbo-proxy Plugin allows you to proxy HTTP requests to Apache Dubbo .
IMPORTANT

route.upstream_multiplex_count: Maximum number of multiplex requests in an upstream connection.

overview:
The http-dubbo plugin can transcode between http and Dubbo (Note: in
Dubbo 2.x, the serialization type of the upstream service must be fastjson).

route.max_req_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes buffered into memory. Requests with a larger body are rejected.
route.params_type_desc: Description of the Dubbo service method signature
route.serialization_header_key: If serialization_header_key is set, the plugin will read this request header to determine if the body has already been serialized according to the Dubbo protocol. If the value of this request header is true, the plugin will not modify the body content and will directly consider it as Dubbo request parameters. If it is false, the developer is required to pass parameters in the format of Dubbo’s generic invocation, and the plugin will handle serialization. Note: Due to differences in precision between Lua and Java, serialization by the plugin may lead to parameter precision discrepancies.
route.serialized: Same as serialization_header_key . Priority is lower than serialization_header_key .

overview: The mqtt-proxy Plugin is an L4 Plugin that supports proxying and load balancing MQTT requests to MQTT servers. It supports MQTT versions 3.1.* and 5.0 . The Plugin must be configured on a stream Route, and APISIX should enable L4 traffic proxying.

route.protocol_level: Level of the protocol. It should be 4 for MQTT 3.1.* and 5 for MQTT 5.0 .

overview: The kafka-proxy plugin can be used to configure advanced parameters for the kafka upstream of Apache APISIX, such as SASL authentication.

route.sasl: SASL/PLAIN authentication configuration, when this configuration exists, turn on SASL authentication; this object will contain two parameters username and password, they must be configured.

overview: After enabling the batch-requests plugin, users can assemble multiple requests into one request and send them to the gateway. The gateway will parse the corresponding requests from the request body and then individually encapsulate them into separate requests. Instead of the user initiating multiple HTTP requests to the gateway, the gateway will use the HTTP pipeline method, go through several stages such as route matching, forwarding to the corresponding upstream, and then return the combined results to the client after merging.

route.timeout: Timeout in ms.
route.ssl_verify: Set to verify if the SSL certs matches the hostname.

overview: The redirect Plugin can be used to configure redirects.

route.http_to_https: When set to true and the request is HTTP, it will be redirected to HTTPS with the same URI with a 301 status code.  Note the querystring from the raw URI will also be contained in the Location header.
route.uri: URI to redirect to. Can contain Nginx variables. For example, /test/index.html , $uri/index.html , ${uri}/index.html , https://example.com/foo/bar . If you refer to a variable name that doesn’t exist, instead of throwing an error, it will treat it as an empty variable.
route.regex_uri: Match the URL from client with a regular expression and redirect. If it doesn’t match, the request will be forwarded to the Upstream. Only either of uri or regex_uri can be used at a time. For example, [” ^/iresty/(. )/(. )/(.*)”, ”/$1-$2-$3”], where the first element is the regular expression to match and the second element is the URI to redirect to. APISIX only support one regex_uri currently, so the length of the regex_uri array is 2 .
route.encode_uri: When set to true the URI in the Location header will be encoded as per RFC3986 .
route.append_query_string: When set to true , adds the query string from the original request to the Location header. If the configured uri or regex_uri already contains a query string, the query string from the request will be appended to it with an & . Do not use this if you have already handled the query string (for example, with an Nginx variable $request_uri ) to avoid duplicates.

overview: The echo Plugin is to help users understand how they can develop an APISIX Plugin.
This Plugin addresses common functionalities in phases like init, rewrite, access, balancer, header filter, body filter and log.

route.before_body: Body to use before the filter phase.
route.body: Body that replaces the Upstream response.
route.after_body: Body to use after the modification phase.
route.headers: New headers to use for the response.

overview:
The gzip Plugin dynamically sets the behavior of gzip in Nginx .
When the gzip plugin is enabled, the client needs to include Accept-Encoding: gzip in the request header to indicate support for gzip compression. Upon receiving the request, APISIX dynamically determines whether to compress the response content based on the client’s support and server configuration. If the conditions are met, APISIX adds the Content-Encoding: gzip header to the response, indicating that the response content has been compressed using gzip. Upon receiving the response, the client uses the corresponding decompression algorithm based on the Content-Encoding header to decompress the response content and obtain the original response content.
IMPORTANT

route.types: Dynamically sets the gzip_types directive. Special value "*" matches any MIME type.
route.buffers.number: Dynamically sets the gzip_buffers directive parameter number .
route.buffers.size: Dynamically sets the gzip_buffers directive parameter size . The unit is in bytes.

overview: The brotli Plugin dynamically sets the behavior of brotli in Nginx .

route.types: Dynamically sets the brotli_types directive. Special value "*" matches any MIME type.
route.mode: Dynamically sets the brotli decompress mode , more info in RFC 7932 .
route.lgwin: Dynamically sets the brotli sliding window size , lgwin is Base 2 logarithm of the sliding window size, set to 0 lets compressor decide over the optimal value, more info in RFC 7932 .
route.lgblock: Dynamically sets the brotli input block size , lgblock is Base 2 logarithm of the maximum input block size, set to 0 lets compressor decide over the optimal value, more info in RFC 7932 .
route.http_version: Like the gzip_http_version directive, sets the minimum HTTP version of a request required to compress a response.
route.vary: Like the gzip_vary directive, enables or disables inserting the “Vary: Accept-Encoding” response header field.

overview: The real-ip Plugin allows APISIX to set the client’s real IP by the IP address passed in the HTTP header or HTTP query string. This is particularly useful when APISIX is behind a reverse proxy, since the proxy could act as the request originating client otherwise.
The Plugin is functionally similar to NGINX’s ngx_http_realip_module but offers more flexibility.

route.source: A built-in APISIX variable or NGINX variable , such as http_x_forwarded_for or arg_realip . The variable value should be a valid IP address that represents the client’s real IP address, with an optional port.
route.trusted_addresses: Trusted addresses that are known to send correct replacement addresses. This configuration sets the set_real_ip_from directive.
route.recursive: If false, replace the original client address that matches one of the trusted addresses by the last address sent in the configured source . If true, replace the original client address that matches one of the trusted addresses by the last non-trusted address sent in the configured source .

overview: The server-info Plugin periodically reports basic server information to etcd.
WARNING

route.boot_time: Bootstrap time (UNIX timestamp) of the APISIX instance. Resets when hot updating but not when APISIX is just reloaded.
route.etcd_version: Version of the etcd cluster used by APISIX. Will be unknown if the network to etcd is partitioned.
route.hostname: Hostname of the machine/pod APISIX is deployed to.
route.report_ttl: Time in seconds after which the report is deleted from etcd (maximum: 86400, minimum: 3).

overview:
It’s useful to set arbitrary breakpoint in any Lua file to inspect the context information,
e.g. print local variables if some condition satisfied.

In this way, you don’t need to modify the source code of your project, and just get diagnose information
on demand, i.e. dynamic logging.

route.delay: Time in seconds specifying how often to check the hooks file.
route.hooks_file: Lua file to define hooks, which could be a link file. Ensure only administrator could write this file, otherwise it may be a security risk.

overview: The lago plugin pushes requests and responses to Lago Self-hosted and Lago Cloud via the Lago REST API. the plugin allows you to use it with a variety of APISIX built-in features, such as the APISIX consumer and the request-id plugin.
This allows for API monetization or let APISIX to be an AI gateway for AI tokens billing scenarios.

route.endpoint_addrs: Lago API address, such as http://127.0.0.1:3000 . It supports both self-hosted Lago and Lago Cloud. If multiple endpoints are configured, the log will be pushed to a randomly selected endpoint from the list.
route.endpoint_uri: Lago API endpoint for batch usage events .
route.token: Lago API key created in the Lago dashboard.
route.event_transaction_id: Event’s transaction ID, used to identify and de-duplicate the event. It supports string templates containing APISIX and NGINX variables, such as req_${request_id} , which allows you to use values returned by upstream services or the request-id plugin.
route.event_subscription_id: Event’s subscription ID, which is automatically generated or configured when you assign the plan to the customer on Lago. This is used to associate API consumption to a customer subscription and supports string templates containing APISIX and NGINX variables, such as cus_${consumer_name} , which allows you to use values returned by upstream services or APISIX consumer.
route.event_code: Lago billable metric’s code for associating an event to a specified billable item.
route.event_properties: Event’s properties, used to attach information to an event. This allows you to send certain information on an event to Lago, such as the HTTP status to exclude failed requests from billing, or the AI token consumption in the response body for accurate billing. The keys are fixed strings, while the values can be string templates containing APISIX and NGINX variables, such as ${status} .
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify Lago’s SSL certificates.
route.timeout: Timeout for the Lago service HTTP call in milliseconds.
route.keepalive: If true, keep the connection alive for multiple requests.
route.keepalive_pool: Maximum number of connections in the connection pool.

overview: The ext-plugin-pre-req Plugin is for running specific external Plugins in the Plugin Runner before executing the built-in Lua Plugins.
See External Plugin to learn more.

route.conf: List of Plugins and their configurations to be executed on the Plugin Runner.
route.allow_degradation: Sets Plugin degradation when the Plugin Runner is not available. When set to true , requests are allowed to continue.

overview: ext-plugin-post-req differs from the ext-plugin-pre-req Plugin in that it runs after executing the built-in Lua Plugins and before proxying to the Upstream.
You can learn more about the configuration from the ext-plugin-pre-req Plugin document.
The ext-plugin-post-resp Plugin is for running specific external Plugins in the Plugin Runner before executing the built-in Lua Plugins.
The ext-plugin-post-resp plugin will be executed after the request gets a response from the upstream.

route.conf: List of Plugins and their configurations to be executed on the Plugin Runner.
route.allow_degradation: Sets Plugin degradation when the Plugin Runner is not available. When set to true , requests are allowed to continue.

overview: The acl Plugin provides label-based access control for API routes. It checks consumer labels (from APISIX Consumers ) or external user attributes (from authentication plugins that set ctx.external_user ) against configured allow or deny lists.
The Plugin supports three label value formats:

route.allow_labels: Labels to allow. Keys are label names, values are arrays of allowed label values. At least one of allow_labels or deny_labels must be configured.
route.deny_labels: Labels to deny. Keys are label names, values are arrays of denied label values. At least one of allow_labels or deny_labels must be configured.
route.rejected_code: HTTP status code returned when the request is rejected.
route.rejected_msg: Custom rejection message body. If not set, defaults to {"message":"The consumer is forbidden."} .
route.external_user_label_field: JSONPath expression or plain field name used to extract the label value from ctx.external_user . For example, $..groups (JSONPath) or groups (plain field name).
route.external_user_label_field_key: The label key name used for the extracted value. Defaults to the value of external_user_label_field .
route.external_user_label_field_parser: How to parse the extracted field value. If not set, the Plugin auto-detects the format.
route.external_user_label_field_separator: Separator regex for the segmented_text parser. Required when external_user_label_field_parser is segmented_text .

overview: The ai-cache Plugin caches LLM responses and replays them for later requests that resolve to the same prompt, cutting upstream token cost and latency for repetitive workloads (FAQ bots, document Q&A, translation).
This Plugin supports two cache layers:

route.exact.ttl: Time-to-live, in seconds, of an exact-cache entry.
route.cache_key.share_across_routes: By default the cache is isolated per route. If true, entries are shared across every route that computes the same key.
route.cache_key.include_consumer: If true, scope the cache per consumer so entries are not shared across consumers.
route.cache_key.include_vars: NGINX variables added to the cache scope (for example ["http_x_tenant"] ), isolating entries by their values.
route.max_cache_body_size: Maximum response body size, in bytes, to cache. Larger responses are not cached.
route.cache_headers: If true, emit the following response headers: X-AI-Cache-Status (always), one of MISS , HIT (exact or semantic cache hit), or BYPASS ; X-AI-Cache-Age , the entry age in seconds, on any cache hit; X-AI-Cache-Similarity , the cosine similarity score (0–1) between the incoming prompt and the matched entry, on a semantic cache hit only.
route.fail_mode: Behavior when the request is not a recognized AI request that this Plugin can cache (for example, a request that did not pass through ai-proxy or ai-proxy-multi ). skip : let the request pass through uncached; warn : pass through uncached and log a warning; error : reject the request.
route.bypass_on: Rules that skip the cache entirely (no lookup, no write-back) when any rule matches.
route.bypass_on[].equals: Bypass when the request header’s value exactly equals this string.
route.policy: Storage backend. Only single-node redis is available in this release.
route.layers: Cache layers to activate. exact performs an exact-match fingerprint lookup (L1) and is always active; "exact" must always be present in this array. semantic enables a vector-similarity lookup (L2) that is consulted only on an L1 miss. At least one value is required; values must be unique.
route.redis_username: Username for Redis if Redis ACL is used. For the legacy requirepass method, configure only redis_password .
route.redis_password: Password of the Redis node. Encrypted with AES before being stored in etcd.
route.redis_ssl: If true, use SSL to connect to Redis.
route.redis_ssl_verify: If true, verify the Redis server SSL certificate.
route.redis_server_name: TLS SNI when redis_ssl is true. Defaults to redis_host . When redis_ssl_verify is true the certificate must also match this name, so set it when redis_host is an alias the certificate does not cover.
route.redis_keepalive_timeout: Keepalive timeout, in milliseconds, for the Redis connection pool.
route.redis_keepalive_pool: Maximum number of connections in the Redis keepalive pool.
route.semantic.similarity_threshold: Minimum cosine similarity (equivalently, 1 − distance) required to consider a retrieved vector a match. Requests below this threshold fall through to the upstream.
route.semantic.top_k: Number of nearest-neighbour candidates to retrieve from the vector index. Only the highest-scoring result is evaluated against similarity_threshold .
route.semantic.distance_metric: Vector distance metric. Only cosine is currently supported.
route.semantic.ttl: Time-to-live, in seconds, of a semantic (L2) cache entry.
route.semantic.match.message_countback: Number of trailing user -role messages to include in the embedding input.
route.semantic.match.ignore_system_prompts: If true, system -role messages are excluded from the embedding input.
route.semantic.match.ignore_assistant_prompts: If true, assistant -role messages are excluded from the embedding input.
route.semantic.match.ignore_tool_prompts: If true, tool -role messages are excluded from the embedding input.
route.semantic.embedding: Embedding provider configuration. Exactly one of openai or azure_openai must be specified.
route.semantic.embedding.openai.endpoint: OpenAI-compatible embedding API endpoint URL. Defaults to the public OpenAI API when omitted.
route.semantic.embedding.openai.api_key: OpenAI API key. Encrypted at rest in etcd.
route.semantic.embedding.openai.dimensions: Override the embedding output dimension for models that support it.
route.semantic.embedding.openai.ssl_verify: If true, verifies the embedding service’s certificate.
route.semantic.embedding.openai.timeout: Request timeout in milliseconds for the embedding service.
route.semantic.embedding.azure_openai.api_key: Azure OpenAI API key. Encrypted at rest in etcd.
route.semantic.embedding.azure_openai.ssl_veri: If true, verifies the embedding service’s certificate.
route.semantic.embedding.azure_openai.timeout: Request timeout in milliseconds for the embedding service.
route.semantic.vector_search.redis.index: RediSearch index name used as the vector store.

overview: The ai-lakera-guard Plugin integrates with the Lakera Guard API (v2) to perform ML-based security scanning of LLM traffic at the gateway. It inspects request prompts for prompt injection, jailbreak, PII leakage, content-policy violations, and malicious or unknown links, then blocks or alerts based on Lakera’s verdict so individual backend LLM services do not each have to implement their own guardrails.

Which detectors run and at what thresholds are controlled entirely by the Lakera project policy , selected with project_id . There is no gateway-side detector list; Lakera returns a single verdict per call.

route.api_key: Lakera Guard API key, sent as Authorization: Bearer . The value is encrypted with AES before being stored in etcd, and supports secret references ( $secret:// ) and environment variables ( $env:// ).
route.lakera_endpoint: Lakera Guard v2 endpoint. Override for regional or self-hosted instances.
route.project_id: Lakera project whose policy (detectors and thresholds) to apply. If unset, the account default policy is used.
route.direction: Which traffic to scan. input scans the request prompt; output scans the LLM response; both scans the request and then, only if the request passed, the response. See Scanning direction .
route.action: How a flagged verdict is handled. block denies the request; alert is a log-only shadow mode that passes flagged requests through. This only governs flagged verdicts — Lakera API errors/timeouts are still controlled by fail_open even in alert mode.
route.fail_open: Behavior when Lakera cannot be reached (timeout, connection error, non-2xx, decode failure). false (fail-closed) blocks the request; true (fail-open) allows it. A successful flagged: false always passes.
route.fail_mode: Behavior when the request is not a recognized AI request that this Plugin can inspect (for example, plain HTTP traffic on a Consumer-bound Plugin, or a request that did not pass through ai-proxy ). skip : let the request pass through unchecked; warn : pass through and log a warning; error : reject the request. Distinct from fail_open , which governs Lakera API failures.
route.timeout: Lakera request timeout in milliseconds.
route.ssl_verify: If true , verify the TLS certificate of the Lakera endpoint.
route.reveal_failure_categories: If true , append the matched Lakera detector_type s (with their confidence result) to the deny message returned to the client. The full per-detector breakdown is always requested from Lakera and written to the gateway logs regardless of this setting; this flag only controls client-facing exposure.
route.deny_code: HTTP status code returned when a request is blocked. Defaults to 200 so the body — a provider-compatible chat completion (or SSE) carrying request_failure_message — parses as a normal refusal in client SDKs (matching how Lakera Guard itself returns 200 with a verdict). Set a 4xx (e.g. 403 ) if you prefer blocks to surface as HTTP errors.
route.request_failure_message: Refusal text returned (as the assistant message of a provider-compatible response) when a request is blocked.
route.response_failure_message: Refusal text returned (as the assistant message of a provider-compatible response) when an LLM response is blocked ( direction output or both ).

overview: The data-mask Plugin masks or redacts sensitive fields in request data — query parameters, headers, and body — before they appear in access logs or logger plugins (such as file-logger or http-logger ).
This is useful for preventing credentials, tokens, payment card numbers, and other sensitive information from being written to logs.

route.request: List of masking rules to apply to request data.
route.max_body_size: Maximum request body size in bytes to process. Bodies larger than this value are skipped for body masking.
route.max_req_post_args: Maximum number of URL-encoded form fields to parse when masking urlencoded body data.
route.type: Type of request data to mask. One of query , header , or body .
route.name: Field name to mask. For query and header types, this is the parameter or header name. For body type with body_format: json , this is a JSONPath expression.
route.action: Masking action to apply. One of remove , replace , or regex .
route.body_format: Format of the request body. One of json or urlencoded .
route.regex: Regular expression pattern to match against the field value. Capture groups can be referenced in value as $1 , $2 , etc.
route.value: Replacement value. When used with action: regex , capture groups from regex can be referenced as $1 , $2 , etc.

examples.title: Mask JSON body fields using JSONPath

overview: The dingtalk-auth Plugin integrates DingTalk OAuth 2.0 authentication into APISIX routes. It validates a DingTalk authorization code, exchanges it for an access token, and retrieves user information from the DingTalk open platform. Verified user information is cached in a secure cookie session so that subsequent requests are not interrupted.

route.app_secret: DingTalk application App Secret (client secret). This field is stored encrypted.
route.secret: Key used to sign and encrypt the cookie session (8–32 characters). This field is stored encrypted.
route.redirect_uri: URI to redirect the user to when no valid authorization code or session is present.
route.code_header: HTTP request header name from which to read the DingTalk authorization code.
route.code_query: Query parameter name from which to read the DingTalk authorization code.
route.access_token_url: DingTalk endpoint used to obtain an access token.
route.userinfo_url: DingTalk endpoint used to retrieve user information.
route.set_userinfo_header: When true , the verified user information is Base64-encoded and forwarded to the upstream in the X-Userinfo header.
route.timeout: Timeout in milliseconds for HTTP calls to DingTalk APIs.
route.ssl_verify: Whether to verify the SSL certificate when calling DingTalk APIs.
route.cookie_expires_in: Cookie session validity period in seconds.
route.secret_fallbacks: List of fallback secrets used during key rotation (each 8–32 characters).

overview: The feishu-auth Plugin authenticates requests using the Feishu (Lark) OAuth 2.0 authorization flow. Users are redirected to the Feishu login page when unauthenticated. After a successful login, Feishu user information is stored in an encrypted session cookie and optionally forwarded to upstream services via the X-Userinfo header.

route.secret: Secret used for signing the session cookie (8–32 characters). Must remain stable across restarts.
route.auth_redirect_uri: Redirect URI registered in the Feishu application for the OAuth flow.
route.redirect_uri: URI to redirect the user to when no authorization code is present (i.e. to start the OAuth flow).
route.code_header: HTTP header name to extract the Feishu authorization code from.
route.code_query: Query parameter name to extract the Feishu authorization code from.
route.access_token_url: URL to exchange the authorization code for an access token.
route.userinfo_url: URL to retrieve user information using the access token.
route.set_userinfo_header: When enabled, sets the X-Userinfo request header with Base64-encoded Feishu user information.
route.cookie_expires_in: Validity duration (in seconds) for the session cookie.
route.secret_fallbacks: List of fallback secrets used during key rotation.
route.timeout: Timeout (in milliseconds) for HTTP requests to Feishu endpoints.
route.ssl_verify: When enabled, verifies the SSL certificate when connecting to Feishu endpoints.

overview: The graphql-limit-count Plugin limits the rate of GraphQL requests using a fixed window algorithm. Unlike limit-count , which counts each request as a cost of 1, this Plugin charges the quota by how expensive the query is.
cost_strategy selects how that cost is computed:

route.count: The maximum allowed accumulated query AST depth within the time window. Required if rules is not configured.
route.time_window: The time interval in seconds for the rate limiting window. Required if rules is not configured.
route.key_type: The type of key. var treats key as an NGINX variable. var_combination combines multiple variables. constant uses key as a fixed value.
route.key: The key to count requests by.
route.rejected_code: HTTP status code returned when a request is rejected for exceeding the quota.
route.rejected_msg: Response body returned when a request is rejected.
route.policy: Counter storage policy. local stores the counter in memory on the current APISIX node. redis and redis-cluster share counters across instances.
route.allow_degradation: When true, APISIX continues handling requests if the Plugin or its dependencies become unavailable.
route.show_limit_quota_header: When true, include X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers in the response.
route.group: Group ID to share a single rate limiting counter across multiple routes.
route.redis_host: Address of the Redis node. Required when policy is redis .
route.redis_port: Port of the Redis node. Used when policy is redis .
route.redis_username: Username for Redis ACL authentication. Used when policy is redis .
route.redis_password: Password of the Redis node. Used when policy is redis or redis-cluster .
route.redis_ssl: When true, use SSL to connect to Redis. Used when policy is redis .
route.redis_ssl_verify: When true, verify the Redis server SSL certificate. Used when policy is redis .
route.redis_server_name: TLS SNI when policy is redis and redis_ssl is true. Defaults to redis_host . When redis_ssl_verify is true the certificate must also match this name, so set it when redis_host is an alias the certificate does not cover.
route.redis_database: The Redis database number. Used when policy is redis .
route.redis_timeout: Redis timeout in milliseconds. Used when policy is redis or redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_nodes: List of Redis cluster node addresses. Required when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_name: Name of the Redis cluster. Required when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_ssl: When true, use SSL to connect to the Redis cluster. Used when policy is redis-cluster .
route.redis_cluster_ssl_verify: When true, verify the Redis cluster server SSL certificate. Used when policy is redis-cluster .
route.cost_strategy: How the cost of a query is computed. See Cost strategies .
route.max_cost: Reject a query costing more than this with a 403, regardless of the remaining quota. 0 disables the check.
route.score_factor: Scales the computed cost before it is charged, so a cost model with large numbers still fits a sane quota.
route.resolve_variables: When true, a quantifier passed as a GraphQL variable is read, whether the client supplies its value, the operation declares a default for it ( query Q($n: Int = 100) ), or the schema defaults the argument. Turning it off makes a variable contribute nothing, which lets a client move a fan-out value into a variable and pay less for it.
route.introspection_endpoint: Where to fetch the upstream schema from. Derived from the Service’s upstream when unset.
route.introspection_headers: Headers sent on the schema introspection request, for an upstream whose introspection needs credentials. Nothing is taken from the client request: the schema is cached per Service, so an introspection that varied by caller would let whichever request warms a worker choose the schema every later request is costed against, and would let one caller’s rejected credentials cache a failure that answers 400 to everyone else. Encrypted at rest with the other credential fields.
route.field_path: The weighted position in the schema graph. A lone <GraphQL type> weights every field returning that type; <GraphQL type>.<field> weights that field wherever it is selected; further field segments pin the weight to one chain of selections, as in Query.products.nodes.reviews .
route.add_arguments: Query arguments whose values are added to add_value .
route.mul_value: Multiplies the cost of everything selected under the field.
route.mul_arguments: Query arguments whose values are multiplied into mul_value .
route.name: Name of the decoration.
route.labels: Attributes of the decoration, as key/value pairs.

overview: The graphql-proxy-cache Plugin provides caching for GraphQL query responses. It supports both disk-based and memory-based caching strategies for GET and POST requests.
The cache key is derived from the plugin configuration version, route/service/host identifiers, and the GraphQL query body:

route.cache_strategy: Caching strategy. Use disk to cache responses on disk (via NGINX’s native proxy_cache ), or memory to cache in a shared memory dictionary.
route.cache_zone: Cache zone to use. The value must match one of the zones defined in the static configurations . Use a disk zone with the disk strategy and a memory zone with the memory strategy.
route.cache_ttl: Cache time to live (TTL) in seconds for the memory strategy. For the disk strategy, TTL is controlled by the upstream Expires or Cache-Control response headers; if neither is present, the cache_ttl configured in config.yaml is used.
route.consumer_isolation: If true , partition the cache by authenticated identity. When the request resolves to an APISIX consumer ( ctx.consumer_name ) or carries a remote user ( ctx.var.remote_user ), the identity is prepended to the effective cache key so each consumer gets its own cache namespace. Set to false if you want different consumers to share cached responses.
route.cache_set_cookie: If true , cache responses that include a Set-Cookie header. Only valid for the memory strategy — the disk strategy never caches responses with Set-Cookie (NGINX enforces this). Enable only when the upstream’s Set-Cookie is not user-specific.

overview: The ldap-auth-advanced Plugin adds LDAP authentication to a Route or a Service. Unlike ldap-auth , which binds with a DN assembled from the Consumer configuration, this Plugin searches the directory for the user first, then binds as the entry it found. When consumer_required is disabled, users do not need to be enumerated in APISIX; with the default true , each authenticated user must still map to a Consumer by its user_dn .
On each request the Plugin:

consumer.user_dn: DN of the LDAP user bound to this Consumer, for example cn=Jane Doe,ou=users,dc=example,dc=org . This field supports storing the value in Secret Manager using the APISIX Secret resource.

route.ldap_uri: Address of the LDAP server as host or host:port . When the port is omitted, 636 is used if use_ldaps is enabled and 389 otherwise.
route.base_dn: DN of the subtree searched for the user, for example ou=users,dc=example,dc=org .
route.attribute: User attribute matched against the supplied username, for example uid or sAMAccountName .
route.bind_dn: DN used to bind before searching for the user. When unset, the search binds anonymously.
route.ldap_password: Password for bind_dn . Required when bind_dn is set. The password is encrypted with AES before being stored in etcd.
route.use_ldaps: If true, connect over LDAPS. Mutually exclusive with use_starttls .
route.use_starttls: If true, upgrade the connection with StartTLS. Mutually exclusive with use_ldaps .
route.ssl_verify: If true, verify the LDAP server’s certificate. Requires ssl_trusted_certificate to be set in config.yaml , and the host in ldap_uri to match the host in the server certificate.
route.timeout: Socket timeout in milliseconds.
route.keepalive: If true, return the connection to the pool for reuse instead of closing it.
route.keepalive_timeout: Idle time in milliseconds after which a pooled connection is closed.
route.keepalive_pool_size: Maximum number of connections kept in the pool.
route.keepalive_pool_name: Name of the connection pool. Set this to keep connections that use different credentials in separate pools.
route.size_limit: Maximum number of entries the user search may return. The login attribute is expected to be unique, so more than one match is treated as ambiguous and rejected.
route.time_limit: Time limit of the search in seconds. 0 uses the server default.
route.consumer_required: If true, reject the request with 401 when no Consumer matches the authenticated user.
route.header_type: Scheme word expected in the credential header.
route.realm: Realm in the WWW-Authenticate response header returned with a 401 Unauthorized response.

overview: The mcp-bridge Plugin bridges an HTTP client speaking the Model Context Protocol (MCP) over SSE to a stdio-based MCP server. APISIX spawns the configured command as a backend process and relays messages between the SSE connection and the process’s standard input and output.
WARNING

route.command: Command used to launch the MCP server process, e.g. npx .
route.base_uri: Base URI used to build the SSE and message endpoint paths.

overview: The openapi-to-mcp Plugin exposes an existing HTTP API to Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, such as LLM agents, without changing the API. It fetches the API’s OpenAPI document, generates one MCP tool per operation, and answers the MCP protocol itself. When a client calls a tool, the Plugin sends the corresponding HTTP request to the API and returns the response as the tool result.
The MCP server runs inside APISIX. No additional process or service is required.

route.transport: MCP transport served on the Route.
route.openapi_url: URL of the OpenAPI document. The document is fetched on the first request and the generated tools are cached for an hour. The response must be an OpenAPI or Swagger document with a paths object; anything else is reported as an error on every MCP request.
route.base_url: Base URL of the API the tools call. The path of each operation is appended to it. Supports APISIX variables and NGINX variables , for example http://${http_x_backend} .
route.headers: Headers added to every request sent to the API. Values support variables, for example "Authorization": "Bearer ${http_x_api_token}" .
route.flatten_parameters: When false , the tool input nests parameters under pathParameters , queryParameters and headerParameters . When true , they are placed directly in the input object.

overview: The proxy-buffering Plugin disables nginx proxy buffering for the configured route. When proxy buffering is disabled, nginx streams the upstream response directly to the client without accumulating it in memory or on disk first.
This is particularly useful for:

route.disable_proxy_buffering: When set to true , disables proxy_buffering for this route, enabling streaming responses.

overview: The saml-auth Plugin enables SAML 2.0 (Security Assertion Markup Language) authentication for API routes. It acts as a SAML Service Provider (SP) and integrates with external Identity Providers (IdP) such as Keycloak, Okta, and Azure Active Directory to authenticate users before allowing access to upstream resources.

When a request arrives at a protected route, the Plugin checks for a valid SAML session. If no session exists, it redirects the user to the IdP for authentication. After the user authenticates at the IdP, the IdP posts a signed SAML assertion back to the SP’s Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL. The Plugin validates the assertion and establishes a session for the user.

route.sp_issuer: Service Provider (SP) entity ID/issuer URI. Must match the SP entity ID registered with the IdP.
route.idp_uri: Identity Provider SSO endpoint URL. This is the URL to which SAML authentication requests are sent.
route.idp_cert: IdP’s X.509 certificate in PEM format, used to verify signatures on SAML assertions.
route.login_callback_uri: Request path of the SP’s Assertion Consumer Service (ACS), such as /login/callback . The Plugin handles the IdP’s login response on requests whose path equals this value. It is a path, so the externally visible absolute ACS URL is configured in sp_acs_url .
route.logout_uri: Request path of the SP’s Single Logout (SLO) endpoint, such as /logout . Requests to this path initiate the logout flow.
route.logout_callback_uri: Request path of the SP’s SLO callback, such as /logout/callback . The IdP sends logout requests and responses to this path. Must be registered with the IdP.
route.logout_redirect_uri: URL to redirect users to after a successful logout.
route.sp_cert: SP’s X.509 certificate in PEM format. Used by the IdP to verify requests signed by the SP.
route.sp_private_key: SP’s private key in PEM format, used to sign SAML requests. This field is encrypted at rest.
route.auth_protocol_binding_method: SAML binding method for the authentication request. When set to HTTP-POST , the session cookie SameSite attribute is set to None and Secure is set to true .
route.secret: Secret used for session key derivation. Must be identical on all APISIX nodes to ensure sessions are readable across workers and after reloads. This field is encrypted at rest.
route.secret_fallbacks: List of previous secrets used during key rotation. Allows sessions encrypted with old secrets to remain valid. This field is encrypted at rest.
route.idp_issuers: Issuers accepted on a login response. Every assertion in the response must name one of them. When unset, any issuer signed with idp_cert is accepted. An empty array accepts no issuer, so every login is refused. See Issuer and audience .
route.sp_acs_url: Externally visible absolute URL of the SP’s ACS, such as https://sp.example.com/login/callback . It is sent to the IdP in the authentication request, and the Destination and Recipient of the login response must equal it. When unset, it is built from the request’s scheme, host, and login_callback_uri . See ACS URL behind a proxy .
route.sp_audiences: Audiences this SP accepts. An assertion carrying an AudienceRestriction must name one of them. When unset, only sp_issuer is accepted.
route.clock_skew: Seconds of clock difference tolerated against the IdP when checking NotBefore and NotOnOrAfter .
route.replay_dict: Name of a declared lua_shared_dict that records accepted assertions, so that one assertion cannot log in twice on the same APISIX node. When unset, accepted assertions are not recorded. See Assertion replay protection .
route.replay_ttl: Seconds to record an assertion whose acceptance has no expiry. Assertions with an expiry are recorded until they expire, plus clock_skew , for at most one day or replay_ttl when that is longer. Only used when replay_dict is set.

overview:
The websocket-proxy plugin configures advanced parameters for a route whose upstream.scheme is ws or wss . It currently controls the maximum size of a single WebSocket frame APISIX accepts on
each side of the connection.

By default, APISIX accepts a single frame of up to 65535 bytes from either the downstream client or
the upstream; a larger single frame closes the connection. enable_websocket has no such limit,
since it lets nginx relay raw bytes without parsing frames, but scheme: ws / wss parses every
frame in order to run plugin logic against it, and the underlying library caps a single frame’s size
unless told otherwise. This plugin raises that cap for routes that need to send or receive larger
messages, such as a client uploading a file in one WebSocket message.

route.client_max_payload_len: Max size, in bytes, of a single WebSocket message this route accepts from the downstream client, and the max size it will relay from the client out to the upstream. Left unset, the default of 65535 applies.
route.upstream_max_payload_len: Max size, in bytes, of a single WebSocket message this route accepts from the upstream, and the max size it will relay from the upstream out to the client. Left unset, the default of 65535 applies.
